passages.name: 2025年 Passage One
passages.title: 哪些基础设施改进最能推动电动汽车普及
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与环境
passages.summary: 一项新研究揭示了哪些基础设施改进最能增加道路上的电动汽车数量。研究发现，在住宅区街道而不只是购物中心等中心地段安装充电站，可能带来格外大的好处；沿高速公路增设快速充电站、让出行距离超出单次充电续航里程的人更容易用上补充车辆，也可能大大提升车辆电气化的潜力。在所有这些情境中，住处的充电选择都是关键。特兰西克认为，资金有限时排定优先次序非常重要，而这项研究应该有助于为各级政策制定者提供一些指导。

paras.en: A new study from researchers uncovers the kinds of infrastructure improvements that would make the biggest difference in increasing the number of electric cars on the road, a key step toward reducing greenhouse gas emissions from transportation.
paras.zh: 研究人员的一项新研究揭示了哪些类型的基础设施改进最能增加道路上的电动汽车数量，而增加电动汽车数量是减少交通运输领域温室气体排放的关键一步。

w.m: 产生（最大）影响；起（最大）作用

paras.en: The researchers found that installing charging stations on residential streets, rather than just in central locations such as shopping malls, could have an outsized benefit.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，在住宅区街道上安装充电站，而不仅仅是在购物中心等中心地段安装，可能会带来格外大的好处。

w.m: adj. 格外大的；超乎寻常的

paras.en: They also found that adding on high-speed charging stations along highways and making supplementary vehicles more easily available to people who need to travel beyond the single-charge range of their electric vehicles could greatly increase the vehicle electrification potential.
paras.zh: 他们还发现，沿高速公路增设快速充电站，并让那些需要出行到自家电动汽车单次充电续航里程以外的人更容易用上补充车辆，可能会大大提升车辆电气化的潜力。

w.m: 使……可供（某人）使用；为……提供

paras.en: The findings are reported in Nature Energy, in a paper by associate professor of energy studies Jessika Trancik, graduate student Wei Wei, and others.
paras.zh: 这些研究结果发表在《自然·能源》期刊的一篇论文中，论文作者为能源研究副教授杰西卡·特兰西克、研究生魏伟等人。

paras.en: The researchers developed a new methodology to identify charging solutions that would conveniently fit into people’s daily activities.
paras.zh: 研究人员开发了一种新方法，用来找出能方便地融入人们日常活动的充电方案。

paras.en: They used data collected from GPS tracking devices in cars, as well as survey results about people’s daily driving habits and needs, including detailed data from local areas and more general data from the country as a whole.
paras.zh: 他们使用了从车载GPS追踪设备收集的数据，以及关于人们日常驾驶习惯和需求的调查结果，其中既有来自地方的详细数据，也有全国整体层面较为概括的数据。

paras.en: Greatly increasing the penetration of electric cars into the personal vehicle fleet is a central feature of climate mitigation policies at local and national levels, Trancik says.
paras.zh: 特兰西克说，大幅提高电动汽车在私家车保有量中的渗透率，是地方和国家层面减缓气候变化政策的一大核心要素。

w.m: n. （一国、一地或一家机构拥有的）全部车辆；车队

paras.en: A goal of this study was “to better understand how to make these plans for rapid vehicle electrification a reality,” she adds.
paras.zh: 她补充说，这项研究的目标之一是“更好地理解如何让这些快速实现车辆电气化的计划成为现实”。

paras.en: In deciding how to prioritize different kinds of improvements in vehicle charging infrastructure, she says, “the approach that we took methodologically was to emphasize building a better understanding of people’s detailed energy-consuming behavior, throughout the day and year.”
paras.zh: 她说，在决定如何为车辆充电基础设施的各类改进排定优先次序时，“我们在方法上采取的思路是，着重加深了解人们全天、全年的具体耗能行为。”

w.m: v. 排定……的优先次序；优先处理
adv. 在方法上；从方法论上
建立对……的认识；加深对……的了解
adj. 消耗能源的；耗能的

paras.en: To do that, “we examine how different people are moving from location to location throughout the day, and where they are stopping,” she says.
paras.zh: 她说，为此，“我们考察不同的人在一天中如何从一个地点移动到另一个地点，又在哪些地方停留。”

w.m: 从一个地点到另一个地点

paras.en: “And from there we’re able to look at when and where they would be able to charge without interrupting their daily travel activities.”
paras.zh: “然后据此，我们就能考察他们可以在什么时间、什么地点充电，而不打断日常出行活动。”

paras.en: The team looked at both regular daily activities and the variations that occur over the course of a year.
paras.zh: 该团队既考察了常规的日常活动，也考察了一年当中出现的种种变化。

paras.en: “The longitudinal view is important for capturing the different kinds of trips that a driver makes over time, so that we can determine the kinds of charging infrastructure needed to support vehicle electrification,” Wei says.
paras.zh: 魏伟说：“纵向视角对于捕捉驾驶者在一段时间内的各类出行十分重要，这样我们就能确定支持车辆电气化需要哪些类型的充电基础设施。”

w.m: adj. 纵向的；长期追踪的
在一段时间内；随着时间推移

paras.en: While the vast majority of people’s daily driving needs can be met by the range provided by existing lower-cost electric cars, as Trancik and her colleagues have reported, there are typically a few times when people need to drive much farther.
paras.zh: 正如特兰西克和她的同事们此前报告过的，虽然现有较便宜的电动汽车所提供的续航里程，就能满足人们绝大部分的日常驾驶需求，但通常总有那么几次，人们需要开得远得多。

w.m: adj. 成本较低的；较便宜的

paras.en: Or, they may need to make more short trips than usual in a day, with little time to stop and recharge.
paras.zh: 又或者，他们可能需要在一天之内跑比平时更多的短途，几乎没有时间停下来充电。

w.m: adj. 很少的；几乎没有的

paras.en: These “high-energy days,” as the researchers call them, when drivers are consuming more than the usual amount of energy for their transportation needs, may only happen a handful of times per year, but they can be the deciding factor in people’s decision making about whether to go electric.
paras.zh: 研究人员所说的这些“高能耗日”，即驾驶者为满足出行需求而消耗的能源比平时多的日子，一年或许只有寥寥几次，但在人们决定是否改用电动汽车时，它们却可能成为决定性因素。

w.m: adj. 高能耗的；耗能多的
改用电动汽车；改用电力

paras.en: Even though battery technology is steadily improving and extending the maximum range of electric cars, that alone will not be enough to meet all drivers’ needs and achieve rapid emissions reductions.
paras.zh: 尽管电池技术正在稳步改进，不断延长电动汽车的最大续航里程，但仅靠这一点并不足以满足所有驾驶者的需求、实现快速减排。

paras.en: So, addressing the range issue through infrastructure is essential, Wei says.
paras.zh: 魏伟说，因此，通过基础设施来解决续航问题至关重要。

w.m: adj. 至关重要的；必不可少的

paras.en: The highest-capacity batteries tend to be the most expensive, and are not affordable to many, he points out, so getting infrastructure right is also important from an equity perspective.
paras.zh: 他指出，容量最大的电池往往价格最高，许多人负担不起，因此，从公平的角度看，把基础设施做好也很重要。

paras.en: “There are various ways to incentivize the expansion of such charging infrastructures,” he says.
paras.zh: 他说：“激励扩建这类充电基础设施的方式多种多样。”

w.m: v. 激励；以激励措施推动

paras.en: “There’s a role for policymakers at the national level, for example, for incentives to encourage private sector competition in this space, and demonstration sites for testing out, through public-private partnerships, the rapid expansion of the charging infrastructure.”
paras.zh: “例如，国家层面的政策制定者就可以发挥作用：出台激励措施，鼓励私营部门在这一领域展开竞争，并设立示范点，通过公私合作来试验充电基础设施的快速扩建。”

paras.en: Governments at different levels can also play an important part in driving innovation by businesses, he says, and a number of them have already signaled their support for vehicle electrification.
paras.zh: 他说，各级政府也可以在推动企业创新方面发挥重要作用，而且已有一些政府表明了对车辆电气化的支持。

paras.en: Providing easy access to alternative transportation for those high-energy days could also play a role, the study found.
paras.zh: 研究发现，在那些“高能耗日”让人们能方便地使用替代交通工具，也可能发挥作用。

w.m: 使用……的机会；获得……的途径
adj. 替代的；可供选择的
n. 交通工具；交通方式
adj. 高能耗的；耗能多的

paras.en: Vehicle companies may even find it advantageous to provide or partner with convenient rental services to help drive their electric car sales.
paras.zh: 汽车公司甚至可能会发现，自行提供便捷的租车服务或与租车服务商合作，以此帮助带动自家电动汽车的销售，对自己有利。

w.m: 发现做某事……（it 为形式宾语）

paras.en: In their analysis of driving habits, for example, the team found that the impact of either adding highway fast-charging stations or increasing availability of supplementary long-range vehicles for up to four days a year meant that the number of homes that could meet their driving needs with a lower-cost electric vehicle increased from 10 percent to 40 percent.
paras.zh: 例如，该团队在分析驾驶习惯时发现，无论是增设高速公路快速充电站，还是让人们每年最多有4天能更容易地用上长续航的补充车辆，其效果都是：靠一辆较便宜的电动汽车就能满足自身驾驶需求的家庭比例从10%升至40%。

w.m: adj. 成本较低的；较便宜的

paras.en: This number rose to above 90 percent of households when fast-charging stations, workplace charging, overnight public charging, and up to 10 days of access to supplementary vehicles were all available.
paras.zh: 在快速充电站、工作场所充电、夜间公共充电以及最多10天的补充车辆使用机会全都具备的情况下，这一数字升至家庭总数的90%以上。

w.m: 使用……的机会；获得……的途径

paras.en: Importantly, charging options at residential locations (on- or off-street) are key across all of these scenarios.
paras.zh: 重要的是，在所有这些情境中，住处的充电选择（路内或路外）都是关键。

paras.en: The study’s findings highlight the importance of making overnight charging capabilities available to more people.
paras.zh: 这项研究的结果凸显了让更多人具备夜间充电条件的重要性。

w.m: 使……可供（某人）使用；为……提供
n. 能力；（设施的）功能、条件

paras.en: While those who have their own garages or off-street parking can often already easily charge their cars at home, many people do not have that option and use public parking.
paras.zh: 有自家车库或路外停车位的人往往已经可以在家轻松地给车充电，但许多人没有这种选择，用的是公共停车场。

paras.en: “It’s really important to provide access—reliable, predictable access—to charging for people, wherever they park for longer periods of time near home, often overnight,” Trancik says.
paras.zh: 特兰西克说：“真的非常重要的一点是，无论人们在住处附近的什么地方停车较长时间（往往是过夜），都要为他们提供充电条件——可靠、可预期的充电条件。”

w.m: n. 使用的机会；（获得……的）条件
adj. 可预测的；可预期的

paras.en: That includes locations such as hotels as well as residential neighborhoods, she says.
paras.zh: 她说，这包括酒店之类的地方，也包括住宅区。

paras.en: “I think it’s so critical to emphasize these high-impact approaches, such as figuring out ways to do that on public streets, rather than haphazardly putting a charger at the grocery store or at the mall or any other public location.”
paras.zh: “我认为，重视这些影响大的做法非常关键，比如想办法在公共街道上做到这一点，而不是随随便便地在杂货店、商场或其他任何公共场所装个充电桩。”

w.m: adj. 关键的；至关重要的
adj. 影响大的；高影响力的
adv. 随意地；杂乱无章地

paras.en: The study should help to provide some guidance to policymakers at all levels who are looking for ways to facilitate the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, since the transportation sector accounts for about a third of those emissions overall.
paras.zh: 对于正在想方设法推动温室气体减排的各级政策制定者，这项研究应该有助于提供一些指导，因为在温室气体排放总量中，交通运输部门约占三分之一。

paras.en: “If you have limited funds, which you typically always do, then it’s just really important to prioritize,” Trancik says, noting that this study could indicate the areas that could provide the greatest return for those investments.
paras.zh: 特兰西克说：“如果资金有限——通常总是如此——那么排定优先次序就真的非常重要。”她还指出，这项研究或许能指明哪些领域可能为这些投资带来最大的回报。

w.m: v. 排定优先次序；分清轻重缓急

passages.name: 2025年 Passage Two
passages.title: 女制动员的铁路入行记
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与经历
passages.summary: 作者的生活一路走下坡路时，看到铁路招聘制动员的广告，把它当作改过自新、抽身离开的机会，后来坐在夜行列车的守车里，感到自己到了该在的地方。铁路公司只开设两周的课程，规章手册不断修订，公司主管还会躲在暗处抽查，答不上来就会在个人档案里留下不合格记录。学员结业后还要闯过六十天的试用期，作者曾怀疑自己能否胜任，实习出车时也晕头转向，但她认为自己在沃森维尔枢纽站入行再好不过。

paras.en: I had been hanging around for a few years with a very party-time crowd, and my life was on a downward slide.
paras.zh: 我跟一帮成天派对狂欢的人已经混了几年，生活一路走下坡路。

w.m: adj. 成天派对狂欢的；寻欢作乐的

paras.en: I had gotten a Ph.D. and a divorce simultaneously.
paras.zh: 我拿到博士学位的同时，也离了婚。

paras.en: The fancy academic job never materialized.
paras.zh: 那份光鲜的学术工作始终没有着落。

w.m: v. （期待之事）成为现实；实现

paras.en: Soon I was playing flute in a street band, eating donated sandwiches, and spending every night in clubs dancing the night away.
paras.zh: 很快，我就在一支街头乐队里吹长笛，吃别人捐的三明治，每晚都泡在夜店里，一跳就是一整夜。

paras.en: In a few years I was living in the mountains in a shack, and none of my friends worked.
paras.zh: 几年后，我住在山里的一间棚屋里，朋友中没有一个人上班。

paras.en: When I saw the ad in the Sunday paper—BRAKEMEN WANTED—I thought of it as a chance to clean up my act and to get away.
paras.zh: 我在周日的报纸上看到一则广告——“招聘制动员”，便把它看作一个改过自新、抽身离开的机会。

w.m: adj. （广告用语）招聘的；征求的

paras.en: I felt that by doing work this dangerous, I would have to make a decision to live, to protect myself.
paras.zh: 我觉得，干这么危险的工作，我就不得不下决心活下去，保护好自己。

paras.en: I would have to choose to stay alive every day, to hang on to the sides of those freight cars for dear life.
paras.zh: 我每天都得选择保住性命，拼命抓牢那些货车车厢的侧面。

paras.en: The railroad transformed the metaphor of my life.
paras.zh: 铁路彻底改变了我人生的隐喻。

paras.en: Nine thousand tons moving at sixty miles an hour into the fearful night.
paras.zh: 九千吨，以每小时六十英里的速度，驶进令人生畏的黑夜。

w.m: adj. 令人生畏的；可怕的

paras.en: I now would ride that image, trying to stay alive within it.
paras.zh: 从此，我要乘上这个意象，努力在其中活下去。

paras.en: I know that later, when I sat behind the moving train in the darkness of the caboose (供列车员休息的车厢), window open and the unknown fragrances of the land filling the space, the blackness of the night was my friend.
paras.zh: 我知道，后来我坐在行驶的列车尾部，守车里一片黑暗，车窗敞开，大地上不知名的芬芳弥漫其间，那时，漆黑的夜就是我的朋友。

paras.en: It felt good to be powerless and carried along by the destiny of that motion.
paras.zh: 无能为力，任由那运动的宿命带着自己向前，感觉真好。

w.m: adj. 无能为力的；无力掌控的

paras.en: I felt happy and at peace.
paras.zh: 我感到快乐而安宁。

paras.en: I was where I belonged.
paras.zh: 我到了自己该在的地方。

w.m: v. 应在（某处）；适合待在

paras.en: The railroad didn’t believe in lengthy formal training.
paras.zh: 铁路公司并不推崇冗长的正规培训。

paras.en: They offered a two-week class which covered the book of rules, a three-hundred-page document with a dual purpose—to keep trains from running into one another and to prevent any situation in which the company might get sued.
paras.zh: 他们开设了一门为期两周的课程，讲授规章手册——一份三百页的文件，有双重目的：一是防止列车相互碰撞，二是防止出现任何可能让公司遭到起诉的情况。

paras.en: Rules of the road which you had to learn were mixed in with rules which you had to ignore in order to get the work done.
paras.zh: 你必须掌握的行车规则，跟那些为了把活儿干完而必须置之不理的规则混杂在一起。

paras.en: But you had to know that you were ignoring a rule so that in the winter, when company officials had time to sneak around testing, you could work by the book.
paras.zh: 但你必须清楚自己是在无视某条规则，这样一来，到了冬天公司主管有空偷偷摸摸四处抽查的时候，你就能照章办事。

paras.en: The rulebook was also in a continuous state of revision.
paras.zh: 规章手册还一直处于不断修订之中。

paras.en: Revisions appeared in the timetable which you carried with you at all times.
paras.zh: 修订内容会登在时刻表上，这份时刻表你随时都带在身上。

paras.en: Further revisions appeared in regular timetable bulletins which were posted at work.
paras.zh: 更多的修订则登在定期发布的时刻表公告上，这些公告张贴在单位里。

paras.en: Soon your rulebook resembled a scrapbook, with paragraphs crossed out, pages pasted in, and notes on changes which were then crossed out and changed weeks later.
paras.zh: 很快，你的规章手册就像一本剪贴簿：有的段落划掉了，有的页面是贴进去的，还写着关于改动的注释，而几周后这些注释又被划掉、重新改过。

paras.en: It drove you crazy.
paras.zh: 这能把人逼疯。

paras.en: You always had to be on the lookout for a company official hiding in the bushes while you did your work.
paras.zh: 干活的时候，你总得提防躲在灌木丛里的公司主管。

paras.en: This individual would pop out and ask you questions about the latest rule revisions.
paras.zh: 这个人会突然冒出来，问你一些有关最新规章修订的问题。

paras.en: A notation of failure would then appear in your personal file.
paras.zh: 随后，你的个人档案里就会出现一条不合格记录。

paras.en: These notations were referred to as “Brownies,” named after the official who devised the railroad demerit system.
paras.zh: 这些记录被称为“布朗尼”，得名于设计出铁路记过制度的那位主管。

w.m: n. 布朗尼（此处指记过记录，得名于其设计者布朗）

paras.en: As trainmen were fond of pointing out, however, there was no merit system to go with it.
paras.zh: 然而，正如列车员们喜欢指出的那样，并没有一套记功制度与之配套。

w.m: n. 列车员（列车班组成员）

paras.en: Out of seventeen student brakemen three of us were women.
paras.zh: 十七名实习制动员中，我们有三人是女性。

w.m: 实习制动员；见习制动员

paras.en: This was a large percentage, comparatively.
paras.zh: 相对而言，这是个很高的比例。

w.m: adv. 相对而言；比较而言

paras.en: The first women had been hired two years before, and they were around to give us advice.
paras.zh: 第一批女性是两年前招进来的，她们都还在，能给我们出主意。

paras.en: The point was to get through the class, and get over the probationary period known as the “derail.”
paras.zh: 要紧的是通过这门课，再闯过那段被称为“脱轨器”的试用期。

w.m: n. （铁路）脱轨器（此处为试用期的俗称）

paras.en: Then you were in the union and a railroader for life.
paras.zh: 然后你就是工会会员，一辈子都是铁路人了。

paras.en: Getting over the derail took sixty days, and if either the crews you worked with or the company officers had a complaint, you were out.
paras.zh: 要闯过“脱轨器”这一关需要六十天；无论是和你共事的班组，还是公司主管，只要有意见，你就出局了。

w.m: n. （铁路）脱轨器（此处为试用期的俗称）
n. （列车）班组；全体工作人员

paras.en: At the end of two weeks of classroom instruction, you bought a railroad watch, they gave you switch keys and a two-dollar lantern, and you marked up as extra board brakemen.
paras.zh: 两周的课堂教学结束后，你买上一块铁路表，他们会发给你道岔钥匙和一盏两美元的提灯，然后你就登记上岗，成为候补制动员。

w.m: 铁路表（铁路员工使用的标准计时表）
（铁路行话）登记待班；报到上岗

paras.en: On the last day of class, they took us down to the freightyard to grapple with the equipment.
paras.zh: 课程的最后一天，他们带我们去货运场，跟那些设备较劲。

paras.en: We practiced getting on and off moving cars, climbing the ladders and cranking down the handbrakes, changing the eighty-five-pound knuckles that joined the cars together, and hand and lantern signals.
paras.zh: 我们练习上下行驶中的车厢，爬梯子，摇紧手闸，更换把车厢连接起来的八十五磅重的车钩钩舌，还练习手势信号和提灯信号。

paras.en: These signals were the way members of the crew talked to each other, and they were an art form.
paras.zh: 这些信号是班组成员彼此交谈的方式，也是一种艺术形式。

w.m: n. （列车）班组；全体工作人员

paras.en: An old head could practically order a pizza from a half mile away.
paras.zh: 老手隔着半英里简直都能点份比萨。

paras.en: You would see lights, arcs and circles, stabs of light.
paras.zh: 你会看到灯光、弧线、圆圈，还有一道道骤然闪出的光。

paras.en: It would repeat.
paras.zh: 信号会重复一遍。

paras.en: You would stand there confused.
paras.zh: 你会站在那里，一头雾水。

w.m: adj. 困惑的；不知所措的

paras.en: Finally you would walk down the track and find the foreman in a deep state of disgust.
paras.zh: 最后，你会沿着铁轨走过去，发现领班厌恶至极。

paras.en: “I told you to hang three cars, let two go to the runaround, one to the main, go through the crossovers, and line behind.
paras.zh: “我叫你挂三节车，放两节去绕行线，一节去正线，走渡线，再把身后的道岔扳回去。

w.m: n. （铁路）绕行线（供机车绕到车列另一端的侧线）
n. （铁路）渡线（连接两条平行轨道的线路）
（铁路行话）把身后的道岔扳回原位

paras.en: Now can’t you read a signal, dummy?”
paras.zh: 我说，你就不会看信号吗，笨蛋？”

w.m: adv. （用于引起注意或表示不满）我说；喂

paras.en: The day after our practice session, I got into my car and tried to roll the window down.
paras.zh: 练习课后的第二天，我坐进自己的车里，试着把车窗摇下来。

paras.en: My arms didn’t work.
paras.zh: 我的胳膊不听使唤了。

w.m: v. （身体部位）正常运转；起作用

paras.en: This was my first moment of doubt about being able to do the job.
paras.zh: 这是我第一次怀疑自己能否胜任这份工作。

paras.en: It was hard to get the upper-body strength required to hang on and ride for long distances on the side of cars.
paras.zh: 要紧紧扒住车厢侧面、随车行进很长的距离，就需要上身有力量，而这种力量很难练出来。

paras.en: Terror at falling beneath the wheels was a big motivator, however.
paras.zh: 不过，对跌落到车轮底下的恐惧，是一股强大的动力。

paras.en: Terror and ridicule.
paras.zh: 恐惧，还有嘲笑。

paras.en: There was a lot of both during the probationary period and the student trips.
paras.zh: 在试用期和实习出车期间，这两样都多得是。

paras.en: On student trips we tagged along with a regular crew and tried to learn something.
paras.zh: 实习出车时，我们跟着一个正式班组，努力学点东西。

w.m: n. （列车）班组；全体工作人员

paras.en: To me, what we were doing made no sense whatsoever.
paras.zh: 在我看来，我们干的这些事完全莫名其妙。

paras.en: Just getting used to the equipment had me so disorientated that I had no idea where we had gone or how the crew did anything.
paras.zh: 光是适应那些设备，就把我弄得晕头转向，既不知道我们去过哪里，也不知道班组的活儿都是怎么干的。

w.m: adj. 晕头转向的；迷失方向的
n. （列车）班组；全体工作人员

paras.en: One of the crew suggested to me that I go to a toy store and look at the model trains, to see how switches work.
paras.zh: 班组里有个人建议我去玩具店看看模型火车，好弄明白道岔是怎么工作的。

w.m: n. （列车）班组；全体工作人员
建议（that 从句中动词用原形）

paras.en: They say, though, that whatever you start out doing railroading, it gets imprinted, and that’s what you are most comfortable doing from then on.
paras.zh: 不过，人们说，干铁路这一行，无论你起步时做的是什么，都会在你身上深深打下烙印，从那以后，你做那件事最得心应手。

w.m: adj. 自在的；得心应手的

paras.en: I couldn’t have picked a better place to break in than Watsonville Junction.
paras.zh: 要说入行的地方，我再也挑不出比沃森维尔枢纽站更好的了。

paras.en: It was old-time, local-freight, full-crew switching.
paras.zh: 那里的活儿是老派的调车作业：地方货运，满员班组。

w.m: 地方货运（沿途各站停靠的短途货运）

paras.en: Kicking cars and passing signs.
paras.zh: 溜放车厢，传递信号。

w.m: （铁路）溜放车厢（推动车厢后摘钩，让其自行滑行）

paras.en: The basic stuff that you have to learn at first or you never get no matter how long you’re out here.
paras.zh: 这是基本功，你得一开始就学会，不然不管在这儿干多久，你都永远弄不懂。

w.m: 在这儿（指在这一行干活）

passages.name: 2025年 Passage Three
passages.title: 与虎同舟熬过海上风暴
passages.summary: 一天下午风暴来临，涌浪如山，“我”放出两只海锚，救生艇一次次冲上浪峰、又落进浪谷，船头处泡沫和浪花迸溅，“我”每次都被浇透。一道涌浪让船头没入水下、小艇灌满了水，面对“死于水”还是“死于兽口”的选择，“我”选择了后者：跳上防水布朝船尾展开，把老虎理查德·帕克关在里面，又挤到防水布下，从艇内尽力把它固定住。此后直到夜里，小艇起落不停，“我”浑身湿透、冻得发僵，还受了伤，恐惧变得单调乏味，取而代之的是麻木和彻底的放弃；夜里某个时候风暴过去，“我”透过防水布的裂口瞥见了满天星斗。

paras.en: The storm came on slowly one afternoon.
paras.zh: 一天下午，风暴缓缓来临。

paras.en: The clouds looked as if they were stumbling along before the wind, frightened.
paras.zh: 云朵看上去像是被风推着，跌跌撞撞地往前走，一副惊恐的样子。

w.m: 被风推着；顺风（航海用语）

paras.en: The sea took its cue.
paras.zh: 大海得了暗示，也跟着动了起来。

w.m: 得到暗示而行动；跟着学样

paras.en: It started rising and falling in a manner that made my heart sink.
paras.zh: 海面开始起伏，那架势让我的心直往下沉。

w.m: 使某人的心一沉；令人沮丧不安

paras.en: I took in the net.
paras.zh: 我把网收了回来。

paras.en: Oh, you should have seen that landscape!
paras.zh: 啊，你真该看看那番景象！

paras.en: What I had seen up till now were mere hillocks of water.
paras.zh: 直到此时，我所见过的都还只是些小水丘。

paras.en: These swells were truly mountains.
paras.zh: 这些涌浪，真真正正是一座座大山。

paras.en: The valleys we found ourselves in were so deep they were gloomy.
paras.zh: 我们身陷的浪谷那么深，深得一片昏暗。

w.m: adv. 如此；那么（so…（that）结构，此处省略 that）

paras.en: Their sides were so steep the lifeboat started sliding down them, nearly surfing.
paras.zh: 浪谷两侧的坡那么陡，救生艇开始顺坡下滑，几乎是在冲浪了。

w.m: adv. 如此；那么（so…（that）结构，此处省略 that）

paras.en: The raft was getting exceptionally rough treatment, being pulled out of the water and dragged along bouncing.
paras.zh: 木筏被折腾得格外厉害：它被拽出水面，一路蹦跳着被拖着走。

paras.en: I deployed both sea anchors fully, at different lengths so that they would not interfere with each other.
paras.zh: 我把两只海锚都完全放了出去，绳长各不相同，这样它们就不会相互干扰。

paras.en: Climbing the giant swells, the boat clung to the sea anchors like a mountain climber to a rope.
paras.zh: 小艇往巨大的涌浪上爬时，紧紧拽着海锚，就像登山者紧抓着绳索。

paras.en: We would rush up until we reached a snow-white crest in a burst of light and foam and a tipping forward of the lifeboat.
paras.zh: 我们会一路往上冲，直冲到雪白的浪峰，霎时间光亮与泡沫迸发，救生艇向前一倾。

paras.en: The view would be clear for miles around.
paras.zh: 方圆数英里的景象都会一览无余。

paras.en: But the mountain would shift, and the ground beneath us would start sinking in a most stomach-sickening way.
paras.zh: 可是这座山会移动，我们身下的地面会开始下沉，沉得叫人胃里翻江倒海，恶心极了。

w.m: adv. 极其；非常（不表最高级）
adj. 令人反胃的；叫人恶心的

paras.en: In no time we would be sitting once again at the bottom of a dark valley, different from the last but the same, with thousands of tons of water hovering above us and with only our flimsy lightness to save us.
paras.zh: 转眼间，我们又会坐在一道幽暗的浪谷底部，它和上一道不同，却又一模一样；数千吨海水悬在我们头顶，能救我们的，只有我们那份单薄的轻盈。

w.m: 数以千计的；成千上万的

paras.en: The land would move once more, the sea-anchor ropes would snap to tautness, and the roller coaster would start again.
paras.zh: 大地会再次移动，海锚绳会啪地绷紧，过山车又会开动起来。

w.m: v. 啪地一下（猛然）变成（某状态）；突然折断

paras.en: The sea anchors did their job well—in fact, nearly too well.
paras.zh: 海锚的活儿干得很好——事实上，几乎好过了头。

paras.en: Every swell at its crest wanted to take us for a tumble, but the anchors, beyond the crest, heaved mightily and pulled us through, but at the expense of pulling the front of the boat down.
paras.zh: 每一道涌浪到了浪峰处，都想让我们栽个跟头；但海锚已在浪峰另一侧，它们猛力一拽，把我们拖了过去，代价却是把船头往下拉。

paras.en: The result was an explosion of foam and spray at the bow.
paras.zh: 结果，船头处泡沫和浪花轰然炸开。

paras.en: I was soaked through and through each time.
paras.zh: 每一次我都被浇得从里到外湿个透。

paras.en: Then a swell came up that was particularly intent on taking us along.
paras.zh: 接着来了一道涌浪，它尤其执意要把我们卷走。

paras.en: This time the bow vanished underwater.
paras.zh: 这一次，船头消失在了水下。

paras.en: I was shocked and chilled and scared witless.
paras.zh: 我又惊又冷，吓得魂飞魄散。

w.m: 吓得魂飞魄散；吓得不知所措

paras.en: I barely managed to hold on.
paras.zh: 我勉强才抓牢，没有松手。

paras.en: The boat was swamped.
paras.zh: 小艇里灌满了水。

paras.en: I heard Richard Parker roar.
paras.zh: 我听见理查德·帕克一声咆哮。

paras.en: I felt death was upon us.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们死到临头了。

paras.en: The only choice left to me was death by water or death by animal.
paras.zh: 留给我的选择只有一个：要么死于水，要么死于兽口。

w.m: 留给某人的；某人剩下的

paras.en: I chose death by animal.
paras.zh: 我选择了死于兽口。

paras.en: While we sank down the back of the swell, I jumped onto the tarpaulin (防水布) and unrolled it towards the stern, closing in Richard Parker.
paras.zh: 我们顺着涌浪的背面往下沉时，我跳上防水布，把它朝船尾展开，将理查德·帕克关在了里面。

paras.en: If he protested, I did not hear him.
paras.zh: 即便他表示过抗议，我也没有听见。

paras.en: Faster than a sewing machine working a piece of cloth, I hooked down the tarpaulin on both sides of the boat.
paras.zh: 我比缝纫机缝一块布还要快，把小艇两侧的防水布都钩牢了。

paras.en: We were climbing again.
paras.zh: 我们又在往上攀升了。

paras.en: The boat was lurching upwards steadily.
paras.zh: 小艇颠簸着，持续不断地向上冲。

w.m: v. 颠簸着前进；东倒西歪地移动
adv. 持续不断地；稳定地

paras.en: It was hard to keep my balance.
paras.zh: 我很难保持平衡。

paras.en: The lifeboat was now covered and the tarpaulin battened (用压条固定) down, except at my end.
paras.zh: 此时救生艇已经盖住了，防水布也用压条固定好了，只有我这一头没有。

paras.en: I squeezed in between the side bench and the tarpaulin and pulled the remaining tarpaulin over my head.
paras.zh: 我挤进侧边长凳和防水布之间，把剩下的防水布拉过来盖在头上。

paras.en: I did not have much space.
paras.zh: 我的空间并不大。

paras.en: Between bench and gunnel (船舷边缘) there was twelve inches, and the side benches were only one and a half feet wide.
paras.zh: 长凳与船舷上缘之间有十二英寸，侧边长凳只有一英尺半宽。

paras.en: But I was not so foolhardy, even in the face of death, as to move onto the floor of the boat.
paras.zh: 但即便面对死亡，我也没有鲁莽到要挪到小艇底板上去的地步。

w.m: adj. 有勇无谋的；鲁莽的

paras.en: There were four hooks left to catch.
paras.zh: 还有四个钩子没挂上。

paras.en: I slipped a hand through the opening and worked the rope.
paras.zh: 我把一只手从开口处伸出去，摆弄着绳子。

paras.en: With each hook done, it was getting harder to get the next.
paras.zh: 每挂好一个钩子，下一个就越发难挂。

paras.en: I managed two.
paras.zh: 我设法挂上了两个。

w.m: v. 设法做到；勉力完成

paras.en: Two hooks left.
paras.zh: 还剩两个钩子。

paras.en: The boat was rushing upwards in a smooth and unceasing motion.
paras.zh: 小艇正向上猛冲，动作平稳，一刻不停。

w.m: adj. 不停的；持续不断的

paras.en: The incline was over thirty degrees.
paras.zh: 倾斜角度超过了三十度。

paras.en: I could feel myself being pulled down towards the stern.
paras.zh: 我能感觉到自己正被往下拽向船尾。

paras.en: Twisting my hand frantically, I succeeded in catching one more hook with the rope.
paras.zh: 我发疯似的扭动着手，成功用绳子又挂上了一个钩子。

paras.en: It was the best I could do.
paras.zh: 我也就只能做到这一步了。

w.m: 某人力所能及的极限；尽力了

paras.en: This was not a job meant to be done from the inside of the lifeboat but from the outside.
paras.zh: 这活儿本来就不是要在救生艇里面干的，而是要在外面干。

paras.en: I pulled hard on the rope, something made easier by the fact that holding on to it was preventing me from sliding down the length of the boat.
paras.zh: 我使劲拉绳子，这倒还容易些，因为抓着绳子正好能防止我顺着艇身一路滑下去。

w.m: ……的全长（down the length of 顺着……一路）

paras.en: The boat swiftly passed a forty-five-degree incline.
paras.zh: 小艇很快就越过了四十五度的倾斜角度。

paras.en: We must have been at a sixty-degree incline when we reached the summit of the swell and broke through its crest onto the other side.
paras.zh: 我们到达涌浪顶峰、冲破浪峰翻到另一侧时，倾斜角度想必已达六十度。

paras.en: The smallest portion of the swell’s supply of water crashed down on us.
paras.zh: 这道涌浪所蓄的海水中，最小的一部分轰然砸在了我们身上。

paras.en: I felt as if I were being pummelled (反复猛击) by a great fist.
paras.zh: 我觉得自己仿佛正被一只巨拳反复猛击。

w.m: v. 反复猛击；接连捶打

paras.en: The lifeboat abruptly tilted forward and everything was reversed: I was now at the lower end of the lifeboat, and the water that had swamped it, with a tiger soaking in it, came my way.
paras.zh: 救生艇猛地向前倾斜，一切都颠倒了过来：现在我到了救生艇较低的那一头，先前灌满救生艇的水朝我涌来，水里还泡着一只老虎。

paras.en: I did not feel the tiger—I had no precise idea of where Richard Parker was; it was pitch-black beneath the tarpaulin—but before we reached the next valley I was half-drowned.
paras.zh: 我没有感觉到老虎——我并不确切知道理查德·帕克在哪里；防水布下面一片漆黑——但还没等我们到达下一道浪谷，我就已经被淹得半死了。

w.m: adj. 漆黑的；伸手不见五指的
adj. 淹得半死的；几乎淹死的

paras.en: For the rest of that day and into the night, we went up and down, up and down, up and down, until terror became monotonous and was replaced by numbness and a complete giving-up.
paras.zh: 那天余下的时光，一直到夜里，我们升了又降，降了又升，升了又降，直至恐惧变得单调乏味，取而代之的是麻木和彻底的放弃。

paras.en: I held on to the tarpaulin rope with one hand and the edge of the bow bench with the other, while my body lay flat against the side bench.
paras.zh: 我一只手抓着防水布的绳子，另一只手抓着船头长凳的边缘，身体则平贴在侧边长凳上。

paras.en: In this position—water pouring in, water pouring out—the tarpaulin beat me to a pulp, I was soaked and chilled, and I was bruised and cut by bones and turtle shells.
paras.zh: 我就这样保持着这个姿势——海水涌进来，又泻出去——防水布把我抽打得体无完肤，我浑身湿透，冻得发僵，还被骨头和海龟壳撞得青一块紫一块，划出了伤口。

w.m: 把某人打得稀烂；痛打某人

paras.en: The noise of the storm was constant, as was Richard Parker’s snarling.
paras.zh: 风暴的轰响一刻不停，理查德·帕克的低吼也是如此。

paras.en: Sometime during the night my mind noted that the storm was over.
paras.zh: 夜里的某个时候，我的意识察觉到，风暴已经过去了。

paras.en: We were bobbing on the sea in a normal way.
paras.zh: 我们像平常一样在海面上一起一伏。

w.m: v. （在水面上）上下浮动；一起一伏

paras.en: Through a tear in the tarpaulin I glimpsed the night sky.
paras.zh: 透过防水布上的一道裂口，我瞥见了夜空。

paras.en: Starry and cloudless.
paras.zh: 满天星斗，万里无云。

w.m: adj. 布满星星的；星光灿烂的

paras.en: I undid the tarpaulin and lay on top of it.
paras.zh: 我解开防水布，躺在了上面。

passages.name: 2024年 Passage One
passages.title: 教黑猩猩使用语言的尝试与启示
passages.genre: 说明文 · 语言与动物
passages.summary: 如果人类语言是一种独特的交流系统，其他生物似乎就极不可能听懂它；有些人对动物说话时看样子以为动物听得懂，但通行的解释是，动物只是针对特定的声音做出特定的行为，并不真正理解其中词语的意思。20世纪30年代以来，几对科学家夫妇先后尝试教黑猩猩说英语单词、使用手语或塑料图形：瓦肖学会使用代表一百多个单词的手势，还能把这些形式组合成“句子”，萨拉能用塑料图形造出“句子”并理解复杂结构；但心理学家赫伯特·特勒斯认为，黑猩猩只不过是应人们的要求打出手势，而且往往重复人们所用的手势。作者认为，瓦肖和萨拉显然能借助人类选定的符号系统与人类互动，但同样显然无法在语言方面表现出与两岁儿童相当的水平；两岁儿童具备发展出高度复杂的语音和结构系统以及一套运算程序的能力，从而能产出包含数量可能无限的新颖话语的长篇语篇，正是在这一更根本或更抽象的意义上，我们说语言是人类独有的。

paras.en: If the properties of human language make it such a unique communication system, quite different from the communication systems of other creatures, then it would seem extremely unlikely that other creatures would be able to understand it.
paras.zh: 如果说人类语言的种种特性使之成为如此独特的交流系统，与其他生物的交流系统截然不同，那么其他生物似乎就极不可能听懂人类语言。

w.m: adj. 独特的；独一无二的

paras.en: Some humans, however, do not behave as if this is the case.
paras.zh: 然而，有些人的举动却并不像是这么回事。

paras.en: There is, after all, a lot of spoken language directed by humans to animals, apparently under the impression that the animal follows what is being said.
paras.zh: 毕竟，人类会对动物说很多话，看样子是以为动物能听懂他们在说什么。

paras.en: Riders can say “Whoa” to horses and they stop.
paras.zh: 骑手对马喊一声“吁”，马就会停下来。

w.m: int. 吁（让马停下的吆喝声）

paras.en: Should we treat these examples as evidence that non-humans can understand human language?
paras.zh: 我们应该把这些例子当作非人类生物能听懂人类语言的证据吗？

paras.en: Probably not.
paras.zh: 大概不应该。

paras.en: The standard explanation is that the animal produces a particular behavior in response to a particular sound-stimulus or noise, but does not actually “understand” what the words in the noise mean.
paras.zh: 通行的解释是：动物针对某种特定的声音刺激或声响做出某种特定的行为，但并不真正“理解”这些声响中的词语是什么意思。

paras.en: In an early attempt to teach a chimpanzee to use human language, in the 1930s, two scientists (Luella and Winthrop Kellogg) raised an infant chimpanzee together with their baby son.
paras.zh: 20世纪30年代，在早期一次教黑猩猩使用人类语言的尝试中，两位科学家（卢埃拉·凯洛格和温思罗普·凯洛格）把一只幼小的黑猩猩和自己尚在襁褓中的儿子放在一起抚养。

w.m: 卢埃拉·凯洛格和温思罗普·凯洛格（科学家夫妇）

paras.en: The chimpanzee, called Gua, was reported to be able to understand about a hundred words, but did not “say” any of them.
paras.zh: 据报道，这只名叫古娃的黑猩猩能听懂大约一百个单词，但一个也没有“说”出来过。

paras.en: In the 1940s, a chimpanzee named Viki was reared by another scientist couple (Catherine and Keith Hayes) in their own home, exactly as if she were a human child.
paras.zh: 20世纪40年代，另一对科学家夫妇（凯瑟琳·海斯和基思·海斯）在自己家中抚养了一只名叫维基的黑猩猩，完全把她当成人类的孩子来养。

w.m: 凯瑟琳·海斯和基思·海斯（科学家夫妇）
仿佛；就像（后接虚拟语气）

paras.en: These foster parents spent five years attempting to get Viki to “say” English words by trying to shape her mouth as she produced sounds.
paras.zh: 这对养父母花了五年时间，试图让维基“说”出英语单词，办法是在她发声时设法调整她的口型。

paras.en: Viki eventually managed to produce some words, rather poorly articulated versions of “mama”, “papa” and “cup”.
paras.zh: 维基最终总算说出了几个词，即发音相当含糊的“mama”（妈妈）、“papa”（爸爸）和“cup”（杯子）。

paras.en: In retrospect, this was a remarkable achievement since it has become clear that non-human primates do not actually have a physically structured vocal tract which is suitable for articulating the sounds used in speech.
paras.zh: 回过头来看，这是一项了不起的成就，因为现在已经清楚，非人类灵长类动物实际上并不具备在生理构造上适合发出言语所用声音的声道。

w.m: adv. 在身体上；在生理上
adj. 有（某种）结构的；构造……的

paras.en: Recognizing that a chimpanzee was a poor candidate for spoken language learning, another scientist couple (Beatrix and Allen Gardner) set out to teach a female chimpanzee called Washoe to use a version of American Sign Language.
paras.zh: 认识到黑猩猩并非学习口语的合适对象后，另一对科学家夫妇（比阿特丽克斯·加德纳和艾伦·加德纳）着手教一只名叫瓦肖的雌性黑猩猩使用美国手语的一个变体。

w.m: 比阿特丽克斯·加德纳和艾伦·加德纳（科学家夫妇）

paras.en: This sign language has all the essential properties of human language and is learned by many congenitally deaf children as their natural first language.
paras.zh: 这种手语具备人类语言的一切基本特性，许多先天失聪的儿童把它当作自己天然的第一语言来学习。

paras.en: From the beginning, the Gardners and their research assistants raised Washoe like a human child in a comfortable domestic environment.
paras.zh: 从一开始，加德纳夫妇和他们的研究助理就在舒适的家庭环境中，像对待人类孩子一样抚养瓦肖。

paras.en: Sign language was always used when Washoe was around and she was encouraged to use signs.
paras.zh: 只要瓦肖在场，大家就总是使用手语，还鼓励她使用手势。

paras.en: In a period of three and a half years, Washoe came to use signs for more than a hundred words.
paras.zh: 在三年半的时间里，瓦肖逐渐学会使用代表一百多个单词的手势。

paras.en: Even more impressive was Washoe’s ability to take these forms and combine them to produce “sentences” of the type “gimme tickle”, “more fruit” and “open food drink”.
paras.zh: 更令人惊叹的是瓦肖的这种能力：她能把这些形式组合起来，构成“给我挠痒痒”“还要水果”“打开食物喝”这类“句子”。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；令人印象深刻的

paras.en: Some of the forms appear to have been inventions by Washoe, as in her novel sign for “bib” and in the combination “water bird” (referring to a swan), which would seem to indicate that her communication system had the potential for productivity.
paras.zh: 有些形式看来是瓦肖自己的发明，比如她表示“围嘴”的新颖手势，以及“水鸟”这一组合（指天鹅）；这似乎表明，她的交流系统具有能产性的潜力。

paras.en: At the same time as Washoe was learning sign language, another chimpanzee named Sarah was being taught (by Ann and David Premack) to use a set of plastic shapes for the purpose of communicating with humans.
paras.zh: 就在瓦肖学习手语的同时，安·普雷马克和戴维·普雷马克正在教另一只名叫萨拉的黑猩猩使用一套塑料图形，以便与人类交流。

w.m: 安·普雷马克和戴维·普雷马克（科学家夫妇）

paras.en: These plastic shapes represented “words” that could be arranged in sequence to build “sentences”.
paras.zh: 这些塑料图形代表“单词”，可以按顺序排列起来组成“句子”。

paras.en: The basic approach was quite different from that of the Gardners.
paras.zh: 其基本方法与加德纳夫妇的截然不同。

paras.en: Sarah was systematically trained to associate these shapes with objects or actions.
paras.zh: 萨拉接受了系统的训练，学习把这些图形与物体或动作联系起来。

paras.en: She remained an animal in a cage, being trained with food rewards to manipulate a set of symbols.
paras.zh: 她始终是关在笼子里的动物，在食物奖励下接受训练，学习操作一套符号。

paras.en: Once she had learned to use a large number of these plastic shapes, Sarah was capable of getting an apple by selecting the correct plastic shape (a blue triangle) from a large array.
paras.zh: 一旦学会使用大量这类塑料图形，萨拉就能从一大排图形中选出正确的那个（一个蓝色三角形），从而得到一个苹果。

w.m: n. 一排；一大批（排列整齐的东西）

paras.en: Sarah was also capable of producing “sentences” such as “Mary give chocolate Sarah” and had the impressive capacity to understand complex structures such as “If Sarah put red on green, Mary give Sarah chocolate”.
paras.zh: 萨拉还能造出“玛丽给巧克力萨拉”这样的“句子”，并且具备令人惊叹的能力，能理解“如果萨拉放红在绿上，玛丽给萨拉巧克力”之类的复杂结构。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；令人印象深刻的

paras.en: A psychologist, Herbert Terrace, argued that chimpanzees simply produce signs in response to the demands of people and tend to repeat signs those people use, yet they are treated as if they are taking part in a “conversation”.
paras.zh: 心理学家赫伯特·特勒斯认为，黑猩猩只不过是应人们的要求打出手势，而且往往重复那些人所用的手势，然而人们却把它们看作仿佛在参与一场“对话”。

paras.en: As in many critical studies of animal learning, the chimpanzees’ behavior is viewed as a type of conditioned response to cues provided by human trainers.
paras.zh: 正如在许多批判性的动物学习研究中那样，这些黑猩猩的行为被视为对人类训练员所给提示的一种条件反应。

w.m: adj. 批判性的；持批评态度的

paras.en: Important lessons have been learned from attempts to teach chimpanzees how to use forms of language.
paras.zh: 人们尝试教黑猩猩如何使用各种形式的语言，已经从中汲取了重要的经验教训。

paras.en: We have answered some questions.
paras.zh: 我们已经回答了一些问题。

paras.en: Were Washoe and Sarah capable of taking part in interaction with humans by using a symbol system chosen by humans and not chimpanzees?
paras.zh: 瓦肖和萨拉能否借助一套由人类而非黑猩猩选定的符号系统，参与同人类的互动？

paras.en: The answer is clearly “Yes”.
paras.zh: 答案显然是“能”。

paras.en: Could Washoe and Sarah go on to perform linguistically on a level comparable to a two-year-old child?
paras.zh: 瓦肖和萨拉能否进而在语言方面表现出与两岁儿童相当的水平？

paras.en: The answer is just as clearly “No”.
paras.zh: 答案同样显然是“不能”。

paras.en: In arriving at these answers, we have also had to face the fact that, even with our list of key properties, we still don’t seem to have a non-controversial definition of what counts as “using language”.
paras.zh: 在得出这些答案的过程中，我们也不得不面对一个事实：即便有了我们列出的那份关键特性清单，对于怎样才算“使用语言”，我们似乎仍然没有一个无争议的定义。

paras.en: It has to be fair to say that, in both cases, we observe the participants “using language”.
paras.zh: 这样说肯定是公允的：在这两种情况下，我们都观察到参与者在“使用语言”。

w.m: （这样）说是公允的；可以公平地说

paras.en: However, there is a difference.
paras.zh: 然而，二者是有区别的。

paras.en: Underlying the two-year-old’s communicative activity is the capacity to develop a highly complex system of sounds and structures, plus a set of computational procedures, which will allow the child to produce extended discourse containing a potentially infinite number of novel utterances.
paras.zh: 在两岁儿童的交际活动背后，是一种能力：能够发展出一套高度复杂的语音和结构系统，外加一套运算程序；这将使孩子得以产出长篇语篇，其中包含数量可能无限的新颖话语。

w.m: v. 构成……的基础；隐藏在……背后

paras.en: No other creature has been observed “using language” in this sense.
paras.zh: 人们还没有观察到其他任何生物在这个意义上“使用语言”。

paras.en: It is in this more fundamental or abstract sense that we say that language is uniquely human.
paras.zh: 正是在这种更根本或更抽象的意义上，我们才说语言是人类独有的。

w.m: adv. 独有地；独一无二地

passages.name: 2024年 Passage Two
passages.title: 北极沉船“调查者”号的考古与打捞
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 考古与历史
passages.summary: 加拿大公园管理局的考古学家于2010年在北极班克斯岛的慈悲湾发现了英国皇家海军“调查者”号的残骸，2011年又带着更大的团队重返此地，潜水考察并记录这艘保存得出奇完好的沉船。该船船长麦克卢尔最初奉命寻找并营救富兰克林率领的两艘船，“调查者”号后来在慈悲湾被冰困住，1853年遭到弃置。考古学家原本没有打算打捞文物，但甲板上暴露在外的文物数量出乎他们的意料，留在原地又容易遭到冰山破坏，他们只好临时想办法打捞，并把文物运往渥太华的实验室保护和研究。

paras.en: It was well past midnight this past July and the round-the-clock Arctic sun was shining on Mercy Bay.
paras.zh: 刚刚过去的七月里，时间早已过了午夜，北极昼夜不落的太阳照耀着慈悲湾。

w.m: 远远超过；早已过了（某时刻）
adj. 昼夜不停的；全天候的

paras.en: Exhausted Parks Canada archaeologist Ryan Harris was experiencing a rare moment of rest on the rocky beach, looking out over the bay’s dark, ice-studded water.
paras.zh: 加拿大公园管理局的考古学家瑞安·哈里斯已经筋疲力尽，此刻正在满是岩石的海滩上享受难得的片刻休息，眺望着海湾里浮冰点点的幽暗海水。

w.m: v. 经历；享受（某种状态）
adj. 浮冰点点的；布满冰块的

paras.en: Around him, a dozen red-and-yellow tents lined the shoreline—the only signs of life.
paras.zh: 他四周的海岸线上排列着十二顶红黄相间的帐篷——这是那里仅有的生命迹象。

paras.en: Every day for the previous two weeks, work had started by mid-morning and continued nonstop for 16 hours.
paras.zh: 此前两周，每天的工作最晚上午十点左右就开始，一刻不停地持续16个小时。

w.m: n. 上午十点左右；上午过半时

paras.en: Night and day had little relevance in the murky, near-freezing waters.
paras.zh: 在浑浊而接近冰点的海水里，是白天还是黑夜几乎无关紧要。

paras.en: Along with Parks Canada’s chief of underwater archaeology, Marc-Andre Bernier, Harris has overseen more than 100 dives at this remote inlet of Banks Island in Aulavik National Park, exploring the wreck of HMS Investigator, a British vessel that has sat on the bottom of the bay for more than 150 years.
paras.zh: 哈里斯与加拿大公园管理局水下考古负责人马克-安德烈·贝尼耶一起，在班克斯岛奥拉维克国家公园内这处偏远的小海湾已主持了100多次潜水，考察英国皇家海军“调查者”号的残骸；这艘英国船只已在湾底躺了150多年。

w.m: n. 英国皇家海军舰艇（His/Her Majesty’s Ship的缩写）

paras.en: Harris and a small team of archaeologists had discovered Investigator in 2010 and returned in 2011 with a larger team to dive, study, and document the wreck, which holds a critical place in the history of Arctic exploration.
paras.zh: 哈里斯和一支由考古学家组成的小团队于2010年发现了“调查者”号，2011年又带着一支更大的团队重返此地，潜水考察、研究并记录这艘沉船——它在北极探险史上占有至关重要的地位。

paras.en: Twenty-five feet below the surface, Investigator sits upright, intact, and remarkably well preserved.
paras.zh: 在水面以下25英尺处，“调查者”号直立着，完整无损，保存得出奇完好。

paras.en: Silt covers everything below the main deck, entombing the officers’ cabins, the ship’s galley, and a full library.
paras.zh: 淤泥覆盖了主甲板以下的一切，把军官舱室、船上的厨房和一间藏书齐全的图书室都掩埋在下面。

paras.en: The archaeologists had intended to leave the wreck and its artifacts where they had lain since the polar ship was abandoned, trapped in ice, on June 3, 1853.
paras.zh: 考古学家原本打算让沉船及其文物留在原处——自1853年6月3日这艘极地船只被困冰中、遭到弃置以来，它们就一直躺在那里。

paras.en: Artifact recovery was not part of their original plan, but that plan changed after their first few dives.
paras.zh: 打捞文物本不在他们原定的计划之内，但最初几次潜水之后，这个计划就改变了。

paras.en: The team was instantly surprised by the number of artifacts they saw—muskets (火枪), shoes, and hunks of copper sheathing rested on Investigator’s upper deck, dangled off the hull, or lay haphazardly on the sediment.
paras.zh: 团队立刻对眼前文物的数量感到吃惊——火枪、鞋子和大块大块的铜护层，有的搁在“调查者”号的上甲板上，有的从船体上垂挂下来，有的杂乱地躺在沉积物上。

paras.en: Leaving these artifacts behind in Mercy Bay would have made them vulnerable to the icebergs that regularly scour the bay’s floor, including the ones the six-man dive team had been dodging since their arrival.
paras.zh: 如果当初把这些文物留在慈悲湾，它们就会很容易遭到冰山破坏；这些冰山经常刮擦湾底，其中就包括六人潜水队自抵达以来一直在躲避的那些。

paras.en: Each piece fished from the water was a clue to life at sea aboard a ship during a period of British fervor for Arctic exploration.
paras.zh: 从水中打捞出的每一件物品，都为了解英国北极探险热潮时期船上的海上生活提供了一条线索。

paras.en: The captain of Investigator, Robert McClure, was originally sent to find and rescue two ships, HMS Erebus and HMS Terror, that Sir John Franklin had led into the Arctic in 1845 to discover the long-sought Northwest Passage connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
paras.zh: “调查者”号的船长罗伯特·麦克卢尔最初奉命去寻找并营救两艘船，即英国皇家海军“幽冥”号和“惊恐”号；1845年，约翰·富兰克林爵士率领这两艘船驶入北极，旨在发现人们寻觅已久、连接大西洋和太平洋的西北航道。

w.m: n. 英国皇家海军舰艇
n. 爵士（用于有爵位者姓名前的尊称）

paras.en: Investigator’s voyage ended, without sight or word of Franklin’s ships or crew, when it was set upon by ice in Mercy Bay.
paras.zh: “调查者”号在慈悲湾遭到冰层围攻，航程就此结束，始终没有见到富兰克林的船只或船员，也没有得到他们的任何消息。

paras.en: After 39 months at sea, the listing ship sat, slowly being crushed on all sides, for three frigid years—with no Inuit encounters, no British search parties, and no relief.
paras.zh: 在海上度过39个月后，这艘倾斜的船在严寒中一停就是三年，四面八方都在慢慢挤压它——其间没有遇到因纽特人，没有英国搜救队前来，也没有任何救援。

paras.en: For much of that time, McClure and his crew of 60 were desperate and under constant threat of starvation, until a surprising rescue in the spring of 1853.
paras.zh: 在那段时间的大部分时候，麦克卢尔和他的60名船员都陷于绝望，时刻面临饿死的威胁，直到1853年春天才出人意料地获救。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；时刻存在的

paras.en: Fifty-five men survived the ordeal.
paras.zh: 55人从这场磨难中幸存了下来。

paras.en: In July 2010, after months of study to pinpoint Investigator’s resting place, the actual discovery of the wreck took just a few minutes.
paras.zh: 为精确定位“调查者”号的长眠之处，研究工作持续了数月；而2010年7月，真正发现这艘沉船只用了短短几分钟。

w.m: v. 精确定位；准确找出
长眠之处；（沉船的）所在之处

paras.en: Harris was in the bay in an inflatable boat testing sonar equipment when the wreck came into range.
paras.zh: 当时，哈里斯正在海湾里乘着一艘充气艇测试声呐设备，沉船就在这时进入了探测范围。

paras.en: The four hours of video gathered on that trip showed that the ship was, in essence, frozen in time, protected by the cold water and opaque, light-blocking ice cover.
paras.zh: 那次考察拍摄的4个小时视频显示，这艘船实际上被定格在了时光里，受到寒冷海水以及不透明、能遮挡光线的冰盖保护。

w.m: 定格在某一时刻的；（时间）凝固的

paras.en: It would be a year before they could return with cold-water diving equipment to have a closer, more detailed look.
paras.zh: 他们要过一年才能带着冷水潜水装备重返此地，更近、更仔细地察看沉船。

paras.en: Over that year, the Parks Canada team pored over photographs and examined glowing gold ultrasound images that showed timber from the wreck scattered across the upper deck like matchsticks.
paras.zh: 在那一年里，加拿大公园管理局的团队仔细研究了照片，还查看了一张张闪着金光的超声波图像；图像显示，沉船上的木材像火柴棍一样散落在上甲板各处。

paras.en: They sought and received the blessing for a more intensive exploration of the wreck site from the 136 residents of Sachs Harbour, an Inuvialuit (Inuit from the western Arctic) community on the southwestern tip of Banks Island, the closest permanent community, some 125 miles away.
paras.zh: 他们请求萨克斯港的136位居民准许他们更深入地考察沉船地点，并得到了同意；萨克斯港是因纽维阿卢伊特人（北极西部的因纽特人）的一个社区，位于班克斯岛西南端，是离沉船最近的永久性社区，相距约125英里。

paras.en: In addition to the underwater work to document the wreck, archaeologist Henry Cary led a land-based survey and excavation team of Inuvialuit archaeologists, conservation officers, and park staff.
paras.zh: 除了记录沉船的水下工作外，考古学家亨利·卡里还带领一支陆上勘测与发掘队，队员包括因纽维阿卢伊特考古学家、资源保护官员和公园工作人员。

w.m: adj. 陆上的；以陆地为基地的
n. 工作人员；全体员工

paras.en: It fell upon Cary to shuttle the 8,820 pounds of equipment up to the 74th parallel, including tents, a three-week supply of food, two boats, diving gear, compressors, recording equipment, surveying tools, and 20 barrels for collecting fresh drinking water.
paras.zh: 把这8820磅装备分趟运到北纬74度线的任务落在了卡里身上，这些装备包括帐篷、够吃三周的食物、两艘船、潜水装备、压缩机、录制设备、勘测工具，以及20个用来收集饮用淡水的桶。

w.m: v. 往返运送；分趟运送

paras.en: The archaeologists came prepared for delays, nasty weather, and polar bears—but they weren’t prepared for the number of artifacts that needed recovery.
paras.zh: 考古学家们来时已为延误、恶劣天气和北极熊做好了准备，但对需要打捞的文物数量，他们却没有做好准备。

paras.en: Harris, Bernier, Cary, and their crews had packed cameras, lasers, and measuring tapes to document the sites but fewer items to help them retrieve, excavate, or transfer artifacts.
paras.zh: 哈里斯、贝尼耶、卡里和他们的队员打包带来了相机、激光仪和卷尺，用来记录这些地点，而帮助他们取回、发掘或转移文物的物品则带得少一些。

w.m: n. 一组工作人员；工作队

paras.en: Recovering the wreck’s finds quickly used up their small toolkit for stabilizing artifacts: foam padding, tongue depressors, and gauze bandages.
paras.zh: 打捞沉船中的出水文物，很快就用光了他们那个用来稳固文物的小工具包：泡沫衬垫、压舌板和纱布绷带。

w.m: n. 发现物；出土（出水）文物

paras.en: “We had not really envisioned the number of artifacts that were visible and exposed on the deck.
paras.zh: “我们事先并没有真正预料到，甲板上看得见、暴露在外的文物会有这么多。

paras.en: So, basically, we had to improvise,” says Bernier.
paras.zh: 所以，说白了，我们只能临时想办法。”贝尼耶说。

w.m: v. 临时想办法；即兴应对

paras.en: Someone ripped the lid of a large black storage case off its hinges to use as a cradle to lift a bent and corroded musket from the frigid waters.
paras.zh: 有人把一个黑色大储物箱的盖子从铰链上扯了下来，当作托架，用它把一支弯曲锈蚀的火枪从冰冷刺骨的海水中托了上来。

paras.en: A large food cooler was loaded with a shredded, twisted, oxidized sample of the copper sheathing used by the British navy to reinforce their Arctic fleet for contact with icebergs.
paras.zh: 一个大号食品冷藏箱里装上了一块破碎、扭曲、氧化的铜护层样本；英国海军曾用这种铜护层加固其北极舰队，以抵御与冰山的碰撞。

paras.en: To protect a fragile rectangle of encrusted felt—a novel addition to Investigator that was intended to keep the ship watertight—Harris fashioned a cover out of absorbent chamois (鹿皮), ripped up an old black T-shirt to place underneath it, and sandwiched the artifact between floorboards taken from the boat that had shuttled them between land and the wreck.
paras.zh: 为了保护一块易碎的、结了硬壳的长方形毛毡（这是“调查者”号上新颖的加装物，用来让船身保持水密），哈里斯用吸水的鹿皮做了一个罩子，撕开一件旧的黑色T恤垫在下面，再用从小船上拆下的底板把这件文物夹在中间；那艘小船此前一直载着他们往返于陆地和沉船之间。

w.m: adj. 结了硬壳的；覆有外壳的
n. 增添物；添加的东西
n. 麂皮；（擦拭用的）软鹿皮

paras.en: The artifacts then made a more than 4,000-mile journey, by helicopter and commercial airliner, to the Parks Canada conservation lab in Ottawa, where they are being conserved and studied today.
paras.zh: 随后，这些文物搭乘直升机和民航客机，经过4000多英里的旅程，运抵位于渥太华的加拿大公园管理局文物保护实验室，如今正在那里接受保护处理和研究。

passages.name: 2024年 Passage Three
passages.title: 想出人头地的父母与失败的养鸡场
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 家庭与人生
passages.summary: 叙述者的父亲原本是个农场帮工，对自己的身份地位相当满意；娶了当乡村教师的母亲、有了孩子之后，夫妻俩变得野心勃勃，一心想出人头地，叙述者猜测这也许是母亲的缘故。他们租地养鸡，苦苦挣扎了十年也没能让养鸡场赚钱；叙述者说，如果自己是个阴郁的人，那要归因于他的童年是在养鸡场度过的。后来，一家人放弃了养鸡，决定搬进比德韦尔镇做餐馆生意，带着家当离开了养鸡场。

paras.en: My father was, I am sure, intended by nature to be a cheerful, kindly man.
paras.zh: 我敢肯定，造化本意是要我父亲做个快活、和善的人。

w.m: v. 有意使（成为）；打算让

paras.en: Until he was thirty-four years old he worked as a farmhand for a man named Thomas Butterworth whose place lay near the town of Bidwell.
paras.zh: 直到三十四岁，他都在给一个名叫托马斯·巴特沃思的人当农场帮工，那人的农场就在比德韦尔镇附近。

w.m: n. 农场帮工；农场工人

paras.en: He had then a horse of his own and on Saturday evenings drove into town to spend a few hours in social intercourse with other farmhands.
paras.zh: 那时他有一匹自己的马，每逢星期六晚上便赶车进城，花上几个钟头同别的农场帮工交际往来。

paras.en: In town he drank several glasses of beer and stood about in Ben Head’s saloon—crowded on Saturday evenings with visiting farmhands.
paras.zh: 他在镇上会喝上几杯啤酒，在本·黑德的酒馆里闲站着——每到星期六晚上，那里都挤满了进城来的农场帮工。

w.m: 闲站着；无所事事地待着
adj. 来访的；（从外地）前来的

paras.en: Songs were sung and glasses thumped on the bar.
paras.zh: 酒馆里歌声阵阵，酒杯砰砰地顿在吧台上。

w.m: v. 砰地放下；重重地敲

paras.en: At ten o’clock father drove home along a lonely country road, made his horse comfortable for the night and himself went to bed, quite happy in his position in life.
paras.zh: 十点钟，父亲沿着一条冷清的乡间小路赶车回家，把马安顿好，让它舒舒服服地过夜，自己便上床睡觉，对自己的身份地位相当满意。

w.m: adj. 冷清的；人迹稀少的

paras.en: He had at that time no notion of trying to rise in the world.
paras.zh: 那时，他根本没有想过要设法出人头地。

w.m: 全然没有……的念头；根本没想过

paras.en: It was in the spring of his thirty-fifth year that father married my mother, then a country school teacher, and in the following spring I came wriggling and crying into the world.
paras.zh: 父亲是在他三十五岁那年春天娶的我母亲，她当时是一位乡村教师；到了第二年春天，我扭动着身子，哇哇哭着来到了这个世界。

paras.en: Something happened to the two people.
paras.zh: 这两个人身上发生了某种变化。

paras.en: They became ambitious.
paras.zh: 他们变得野心勃勃。

w.m: adj. 野心勃勃的；有抱负的

paras.en: The passion for getting up in the world took possession of them.
paras.zh: 一股想要出人头地的狂热攫住了他们。

w.m: 对……的强烈渴望；对……的狂热

paras.en: It may have been that mother was responsible.
paras.zh: 这也许是母亲的缘故。

w.m: adj. 是……原因的；应负责任的

paras.en: Being a school teacher she had no doubt read books and magazines.
paras.zh: 身为学校教师，她想必读过书籍和杂志。

paras.en: She had, I presume, read of how some people rose from poverty to fame and greatness and as I lay beside her—in the days of her lying-in—she may have dreamed that I would someday rule men and cities.
paras.zh: 我猜想，她曾读到过有些人如何由贫寒起家，成就声名与伟业；我躺在她身边的时候——那是她坐月子的日子——她也许梦想过，有朝一日我会统治众人、主宰城市。

paras.en: At any rate she induced father to give up his place as a farmhand, sell his horse and embark on an independent enterprise of his own.
paras.zh: 不管怎样，她说动父亲辞掉了农场帮工的差事，卖掉了马，开始独立经营一份自己的事业。

w.m: 劝说某人做；诱使某人做
n. 事业；（有风险的）营生

paras.en: She was a tall silent woman with a long nose and troubled grey eyes.
paras.zh: 她是个高个子女人，沉默寡言，鼻子长长的，一双灰色的眼睛透着忧虑。

w.m: adj. 沉默寡言的；不说话的

paras.en: For herself she wanted nothing.
paras.zh: 为自己，她一无所求。

paras.en: For father and myself she was incurably ambitious.
paras.zh: 为父亲和我，她的野心大得无可救药。

w.m: adv. 无可救药地；治不好地
adj. 野心勃勃的；有抱负的

paras.en: The first venture into which the two people went turned out badly.
paras.zh: 两人投身的第一桩营生结果很糟。

w.m: n. （有风险的）事业；冒险尝试

paras.en: They rented ten acres of poor stony land on Griggs’s Road, eight miles from Bidwell, and launched into chicken raising.
paras.zh: 他们在离比德韦尔八英里的格里格斯路上租了十英亩贫瘠多石的土地，干起了养鸡这一行。

paras.en: I grew into boyhood on the place and got my first impressions of life there.
paras.zh: 我在那片农场上长成了少年，对人生最初的印象也是在那里形成的。

paras.en: From the beginning they were impressions of disaster and if, in my turn, I am a gloomy man inclined to see the darker side of life, I attribute it to the fact that what should have been for me the happy joyous days of childhood were spent on a chicken farm.
paras.zh: 从一开始，那些就是关于灾难的印象；如果说我也是个阴郁的人，倾向于看到人生较阴暗的一面，那么我把这归因于一个事实：本该是我快乐欢欣的童年时光，却是在一个养鸡场上度过的。

w.m: 人生较阴暗的一面；人生的阴暗面

paras.en: One unversed in such matters can have no notion of the many and tragic things that can happen to a chicken.
paras.zh: 不谙此道的人根本想象不到，一只鸡可能遭遇的事有多少、有多悲惨。

w.m: 对……毫无概念；根本想象不到

paras.en: It is born out of an egg, lives for a few weeks as a tiny fluffy thing such as you will see pictured on Easter cards, then becomes hideously naked, eats quantities of corn and meal bought by the sweat of your father’s brow, gets diseases called pip, cholera, and other names, stands looking with stupid eyes at the sun, becomes sick and dies.
paras.zh: 它从蛋里出生，以小小的、毛茸茸的模样活上几个星期，就像你会在复活节贺卡上看到的画中那样，接着就变得光秃秃的，丑得吓人；它吃掉大量玉米和粗粉，那都是你父亲用汗水换来的；它会得上名叫禽舌病、霍乱以及其他名目的病；它站在那儿，两眼呆呆地望着太阳，然后病倒，死去。

w.m: adj. 光秃秃的（没有毛的）；赤裸的

w.h: by the sweat of one's brow
w.m: 靠辛勤劳动；用汗水换来
n. 禽舌病（家禽的一种疾病）

paras.en: A few hens and now and then a rooster, intended to serve God’s mysterious ends, struggle through to maturity.
paras.zh: 少数几只母鸡，偶尔还有一只公鸡，本是要为上帝那神秘莫测的目的效力的，它们挣扎着活到成年。

w.m: 为某人的目的效力；达到某人的目的
adj. 神秘的；不可思议的

paras.en: The hens lay eggs out of which come other chickens and the dreadful cycle is thus made complete.
paras.zh: 母鸡下蛋，蛋里又生出别的小鸡，这可怕的循环就这样完成了。

w.m: adj. 可怕的；糟糕透顶的

paras.en: It is all unbelievably complex.
paras.zh: 这一切复杂得令人难以置信。

paras.en: Most philosophers must have been raised on chicken farms.
paras.zh: 大多数哲学家想必都是在养鸡场里长大的。

paras.en: One hopes for so much from a chicken and is so dreadfully disillusioned.
paras.zh: 人对一只鸡指望那么多，幻灭起来又那么惨痛。

w.m: adj. 幻想破灭的；大失所望的

paras.en: Small chickens, just setting out on the journey of life, look so bright and alert and they are in fact so dreadfully stupid.
paras.zh: 小鸡刚刚踏上生命的旅程，看上去那么伶俐、那么机警，可实际上它们蠢得要命。

paras.en: They are so much like people they mix one up in one’s judgments of life.
paras.zh: 它们和人那么相像，以致把人弄糊涂了，让人对人生都判断不清。

paras.en: If disease does not kill them they wait until your expectations are thoroughly aroused and then walk under the wheels of a wagon—to go squashed and dead back to their maker.
paras.zh: 要是疾病没要了它们的命，它们就会一直等到你的期望被彻底吊起来，然后走到一辆大车的轮子底下——被轧得扁扁的，一命呜呼，回到造物主那里去。

w.m: adj. 被压扁的；被轧扁的
回到造物主那里（指死去）

paras.en: Vermin infest their youth, and fortunes must be spent for curative powders.
paras.zh: 它们幼小时害虫成灾，还得花大笔大笔的钱去买治病的药粉。

w.m: n. 害虫；寄生虫（如虱、蚤）
v. （害虫等）大批出没于；侵扰

paras.en: For ten years my father and mother struggled to make our chicken farm pay and then they gave up that struggle and began another.
paras.zh: 十年间，父亲和母亲苦苦挣扎，想让我们的养鸡场赚钱；后来，他们放弃了这场挣扎，开始了另一场。

paras.en: They decided to move into the town of Bidwell, and embarked in the restaurant business.
paras.zh: 他们决定搬进比德韦尔镇，做起了餐馆生意。

w.m: 开始从事；着手（同 embark on）

paras.en: After ten years of worry with incubators that did not hatch, and with tiny—and in their own way lovely—balls of fluff that passed on into semi-naked pullethood and from that into dead henhood, we threw all aside, packed our belongings on a wagon and drove down Griggs’s Road toward Bidwell, a tiny caravan of hope looking for a new place from which to start on our upward journey through life.
paras.zh: 孵化器孵不出小鸡，一团团小小的绒球——它们自有其可爱之处——进入了半秃的小母鸡期，又从那里进入了死母鸡期；为这些操了十年心之后，我们把一切都抛到一边，把家当装上一辆大车，沿着格里格斯路朝比德韦尔驶去——一支小小的希望车队，要寻找一个新的地方，好从那里出发，踏上我们向上攀登的人生旅程。

w.m: adj. 半裸的（此处指羽毛未长全、半秃的）
n. 小母鸡期（作者仿 boyhood 造的词；pullet 指未满一岁的小母鸡）
n. 母鸡期（作者造的词）

paras.en: We must have been a sad looking lot, not, I fancy, unlike refugees fleeing from a battlefield.
paras.zh: 我们想必是一伙模样凄惨的人，依我看，和逃离战场的难民颇有几分相像。

paras.en: Mother and I walked in the road.
paras.zh: 母亲和我在路上步行。

paras.en: The wagon that contained our goods had been borrowed for the day from Mr. Albert Griggs, a neighbor.
paras.zh: 装着我们家什的那辆大车，是从邻居艾伯特·格里格斯先生那里借来用一天的。

paras.en: Out of its sides stuck the legs of cheap chairs and at the back of the pile of beds, tables, and boxes filled with kitchen utensils was a crate of live chickens, and on top of that the baby carriage in which I had been wheeled about in my infancy.
paras.zh: 车子两侧支棱出廉价椅子的腿；在那一堆床、桌子和装满厨房用具的箱子后部，放着一板条箱活鸡，箱子上面是那辆婴儿车，我还是婴儿时，就曾坐在里面被人推着到处走。

paras.en: Why we stuck to the baby carriage I don’t know.
paras.zh: 我们为什么死守着那辆婴儿车，我不知道。

paras.en: It was unlikely other children would be born and the wheels were broken.
paras.zh: 已经不大可能再有别的孩子出生，而且车轮也坏了。

paras.en: People who have few possessions cling tightly to those they have.
paras.zh: 财物很少的人，会把自己有的那点东西紧紧抓住不放。

paras.en: That is one of the facts that make life so discouraging.
paras.zh: 这便是使人生如此令人沮丧的事实之一。

w.m: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人泄气的

paras.en: Father rode on top of the wagon.
paras.zh: 父亲坐在大车顶上。

paras.en: He was then a bald-headed man of forty-five, a little fat and from long association with mother and the chickens he had become habitually silent and discouraged.
paras.zh: 那时他是个四十五岁的秃顶男人，有点胖；由于长年和母亲以及那些鸡打交道，他已养成了沉默寡言、灰心丧气的习性。

paras.en: All during our ten years on the chicken farm he had worked as a laborer on neighboring farms and most of the money he had earned had been spent for remedies to cure chicken diseases.
paras.zh: 我们在养鸡场的整整十年里，他一直在邻近的农场当雇工，挣来的钱大部分都花在了治鸡病的药上。

w.m: n. 劳工；（干体力活的）雇工

paras.en: There were two little patches of hair on father’s head just above his ears.
paras.zh: 父亲的头上有两小片头发，就在耳朵上方。

paras.en: I remember that as a child I used to sit looking at him when he had gone to sleep in a chair before the stove on Sunday afternoons in the winter.
paras.zh: 我记得，小时候，每逢冬天的星期天下午，他在炉子前的椅子上睡着以后，我常常坐着看他。

paras.en: I had at that time already begun to read books and have notions of my own and the bald path that led over the top of his head was, I fancied, something like a broad road, such a road as Caesar might have made on which to lead his legions out of Rome and into the wonders of an unknown world.
paras.zh: 那时我已经开始读书，有了自己的想法；我觉得，从他头顶上越过的那条光秃秃的小道有点像一条宽阔的大路，就是恺撒或许会修筑的那种路，好让他率领自己的军团走出罗马，进入一个未知世界的种种奇观之中。

paras.en: One might write a book concerning our flight from the chicken farm into town.
paras.zh: 关于我们从养鸡场出逃进城的经过，或许可以写上一本书。

paras.en: Mother and I walked the entire eight miles—she to be sure that nothing fell from the wagon and I to see the wonders of the world.
paras.zh: 母亲和我走完了整整八英里——她是为了确保大车上没有东西掉下来，我则是为了看看世上的种种奇观。

w.m: 世上的种种奇观；世界奇观

passages.name: 2023年 Passage One
passages.title: 澳大利亚的含糖饮料税之争
passages.genre: 说明文 · 健康与公共政策
passages.summary: 澳大利亚出现了开征含糖饮料税的新呼声，遭到食品饮料行业的强烈抗议和政界人士的抵制。支持者认为，这种税针对的产品容易界定，税收收入还可用于资助卫生项目，减轻弱势人群的经济负担。研究数据显示，墨西哥开征该税后含糖饮料购买量下降，墨尔本一家医院在提价试验期间软饮料销量也有所下降。政府则认为现有措施已经足够，行业游说团体称没有证据表明征税能减少肥胖，而且征税会造成就业岗位流失。

paras.en: New calls for Australia to introduce a sugar-sweetened beverages tax have sparked an outcry from the food and beverage industry and provoked resistance from politicians.
paras.zh: 要求澳大利亚开征含糖饮料税的新呼声，引发了食品饮料行业的强烈抗议，也招致了政界人士的抵制。

w.m: adj. 含糖的；加糖增甜的
n. 强烈抗议；公众的强烈反对
n. 政界人士；政治人物

paras.en: But why do health experts keep calling for a sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) tax, and why are politicians and industry resisting it?
paras.zh: 然而，卫生专家为什么一再呼吁开征含糖饮料（SSB）税，政界人士和业界又为什么抵制这项税？

w.m: n. 政界人士；政治人物

paras.en: Sugar taxes vary in design around the world in 26 countries.
paras.zh: 全球26个国家的糖税在设计上各不相同。

paras.en: In Mexico, a 10% tax on sugary drinks was introduced in 2014.
paras.zh: 墨西哥于2014年开始对含糖饮料征收10%的税。

paras.en: When the tax starts in the UK in April, there will be two bands—one for sugar content above 5g per 100ml and a second, higher tax on drinks containing more than 8g of sugar per 100ml.
paras.zh: 英国的糖税将于4月开始征收，届时税率将分为两档：一档针对每100毫升含糖量超过5克的饮料，另一档税率更高，针对每100毫升含糖量超过8克的饮料。

paras.en: In a 2018 statement on nutrition the Australian Medical Association (AMA) urged the government to introduce an SSB tax.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚医学会（AMA）在2018年发布的一份营养声明中，敦促政府开征含糖饮料税。

paras.en: This is significant because the AMA is generally conservative when it comes to health policy and often avoids controversial debates.
paras.zh: 这一点意义重大，因为澳大利亚医学会在卫生政策方面通常态度保守，而且常常回避有争议的辩论。

w.m: adj. 意义重大的；重要的

paras.en: But it now wants a sugar tax “as a matter of priority”.
paras.zh: 但如今，它希望把开征糖税“作为优先事项”。

paras.en: The health minister has made it clear the government will not support it, saying food labelling laws and voluntary codes of conduct to restrict food marketing to children are adequate.
paras.zh: 卫生部长已明确表示，政府不会支持开征这项税，称食品标签法和限制向儿童推销食品的自愿行为准则已经足够。

paras.en: A Labor MP also stopped short of supporting a tax, saying other strategies are needed to promote a healthy lifestyle.
paras.zh: 一位工党议员也没有表态支持征税，称需要采取其他策略来推广健康的生活方式。

w.m: n. 议员（Member of Parliament 的缩写）
没有走到……的地步；未明确（做某事）

paras.en: The Greens, led by former doctor Richard Di Natale, support the tax and have previously proposed a 20% increase to the price of sugary drinks.
paras.zh: 由曾任医生的理查德·迪纳塔莱领导的绿党支持征收这项税，此前还曾提议将含糖饮料的价格提高20%。

paras.en: According to Prof. Tim Gill, from the Boden Institute of Obesity, Nutrition, Exercise & Eating Disorders in Sydney, the strength of an SSB tax is that it targets an easily defined product.
paras.zh: 在悉尼博登肥胖、营养、运动与饮食失调研究所的蒂姆·吉尔教授看来，含糖饮料税的优势在于它针对的是一种容易界定的产品。

w.m: 蒂姆·吉尔教授（Prof. 是 professor 的缩写）

paras.en: “It’s easy to identify sugary drinks and their manufacturers, and you can tax them at their production,” he said.
paras.zh: “含糖饮料及其生产商都很容易识别，而且可以在生产环节对它们征税。”他说。

paras.en: “There are a limited number of sugary drinks producers in Australia.
paras.zh: “澳大利亚的含糖饮料生产商数量有限。

paras.en: A problem for governments collecting taxes can be how complicated it can be.
paras.zh: 政府征税时，一个问题可能就在于征税会有多复杂。

paras.en: If you were to try to tax every sugary food, for example, that would be very complicated to do.”
paras.zh: 比如，假如试图对每一种含糖食品都征税，那做起来就会非常复杂。”

paras.en: The government has previously used complexity as an argument against an SSB tax.
paras.zh: 政府此前就曾把复杂性用作反对含糖饮料税的理由。

paras.en: “But now with the UK, which has a similar consumption culture to ours but with a larger population and more producers, jumping on the bandwagon, that complexity argument doesn’t hold weight anymore,” Gill said.
paras.zh: “但如今英国也加入了这一行列，那里的消费文化与我们相似，只是人口更多、生产商也更多，这种以复杂性为由的论点就再也站不住脚了。”吉尔说。

w.m: 跟风；加入（某一潮流的）行列

paras.en: Bureau of Statistics data shows Australia is one of the 10 highest soft-drink-consuming countries per capita.
paras.zh: 统计局的数据显示，按人均计算，澳大利亚是软饮料消费量最高的10个国家之一。

paras.en: The World Health Organisation recommends adults consume no more than six teaspoons of sugar per day, but the average Australian consumes more than double that.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织建议成年人每天摄入的糖不超过六茶匙，但澳大利亚人的平均摄入量是这一数量的两倍多。

paras.en: A 330ml bottle of Coke contains nine teaspoons of sugar.
paras.zh: 一瓶330毫升的可口可乐含有九茶匙糖。

w.m: n. 可口可乐（Coca-Cola 的简称）

paras.en: A study published in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics found sales of soft drinks in Melbourne’s Alfred hospital dropped 27.6% during a 17-week trial when the price of sugary drinks was increased by 20%.
paras.zh: 发表在《营养与饮食学会杂志》上的一项研究发现，墨尔本阿尔弗雷德医院在一项为期17周的试验中将含糖饮料的价格提高了20%，其间院内软饮料的销量下降了27.6%。

paras.en: Bottled water sales increased by almost the same amount.
paras.zh: 瓶装水的销量则增长了几乎同样的幅度。

paras.en: An analysis of sugary-drink purchases in Mexico conducted two years after the tax was introduced found a 5.5% drop in the first year, followed by a 9.7% decline in the second.
paras.zh: 墨西哥开征该税两年后，一项针对该国含糖饮料购买量的分析发现，第一年购买量下降了5.5%，随后第二年下降了9.7%。

paras.en: While two years is not enough to determine the long-term impact on health, the study found: “These reductions in consumption could have positive impacts on health outcomes and reductions in healthcare expenses.”
paras.zh: 尽管两年时间还不足以确定其对健康的长期影响，但该研究发现：“消费量的这些下降可能会对健康结果产生积极影响，并减少医疗保健开支。”

paras.en: Sugar-sweetened drinks and sugar generally have been associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, tooth decay and bone density problems.
paras.zh: 含糖饮料以及一般意义上的糖，都被认为与肥胖、2型糖尿病、心血管疾病、蛀牙和骨密度问题有关。

paras.en: The Australian Healthcare and Hospitals Association says obesity is the leading cause of preventable death or illness in Australia—above smoking.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚医疗保健与医院协会表示，在澳大利亚，肥胖是导致可预防死亡或疾病的首要原因，排在吸烟之前。

paras.en: But it will take longer-term analysis to see clear evidence of any impact of a tax on obesity levels.
paras.zh: 但要看到征税对肥胖水平有所影响的明确证据，还需要更长期的分析。

paras.en: Lobby groups from the food and beverage industry are powerful.
paras.zh: 食品饮料行业的游说团体势力强大。

w.m: adj. 势力强大的；有影响力的

paras.en: The Australian Beverages Council, the industry’s lobby group, has been fighting against a tax for years.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚饮料理事会是该行业的游说团体，多年来一直在反对征税。

paras.en: It says there is no evidence a tax will do anything to reduce obesity, and that it will cost jobs, which is a frightening message for politicians.
paras.zh: 该理事会称，没有证据表明征税能对减少肥胖起任何作用，而且征税会造成就业岗位流失，这对政界人士来说是个可怕的信息。

w.m: 造成就业岗位流失；使人失业
adj. 可怕的；令人恐惧的
n. 政界人士；政治人物

paras.en: The Australasian Association of Convenience Stores (AACS) described the introduction of an SSB tax in the UK as “lazy”, “flawed”, “discriminatory” and “irrational”.
paras.zh: 澳大拉西亚便利店协会（AACS）把英国开征含糖饮料税形容为“懒惰”“有缺陷”“歧视性”和“不理性”之举。

w.m: adj. 澳大拉西亚的（指澳大利亚、新西兰及附近南太平洋岛屿）
adj. 不理性的；不合理的

paras.en: It has ramped up its campaign to prevent such a tax in Australia.
paras.zh: 该协会已加大活动力度，以阻止澳大利亚开征此类税。

paras.en: Would introducing a sugar tax make Australia a nanny state?
paras.zh: 开征糖税会让澳大利亚变成一个保姆式国家吗？

w.m: 保姆式国家（指政府过度干预个人生活的国家）

paras.en: It depends on whether you believe the food and beverage industry has too much power.
paras.zh: 这取决于你是否认为食品饮料行业势力过大。

paras.en: Health experts argue that through advertising, product placement and political influence, the food and beverage industry has an unfair and non-transparent influence over consumer purchasing habits, and that children especially are sometimes powerless to recognise or resist it.
paras.zh: 卫生专家认为，食品饮料行业借助广告、植入式广告和政治影响力，对消费者的购买习惯施加着不公平且不透明的影响；尤其是儿童，有时无力识别或抵制这种影响。

w.m: adj. 无力的；无能为力的

paras.en: They say an SSB tax would hold the industry to account.
paras.zh: 他们说，含糖饮料税会让该行业承担起责任。

w.m: 让……承担责任；追究……的责任

paras.en: Others argue people need to take personal responsibility.
paras.zh: 另一些人则认为，人们需要自己承担责任。

w.m: 自己承担责任；对自己负责

paras.en: A Deakin University study used economic modelling to show the increase in annual spending on sugar-sweetened drinks under a 20% tax would average $30 a person, but those in the lowest socioeconomic groups would pay $5 a year more than those in the wealthiest groups.
paras.zh: 迪肯大学的一项研究利用经济建模表明，若征收20%的税，每人每年在含糖饮料上的支出平均将增加30澳元，但社会经济地位最低的群体每年要比最富裕的群体多付5澳元。

paras.en: Researchers concluded this was a modest price to pay given the benefits—and that Australia’s lowest socioeconomic group would receive the greatest health benefits.
paras.zh: 研究人员得出结论：考虑到所带来的益处，这点代价并不大，而且澳大利亚社会经济地位最低的群体将获得最大的健康益处。

paras.en: Health experts and advocacy groups say governments could reduce the financial burden on disadvantaged people by using revenue from a tax to fund health initiatives.
paras.zh: 卫生专家和倡导团体表示，政府可以利用税收收入资助卫生项目，从而减轻弱势人群的经济负担。

passages.name: 2023年 Passage Two
passages.title: 我在好莱坞剧本分解公司的半年
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 职场与娱乐业
passages.summary: 1983年，作者应聘到洛杉矶的Breakdown Services有限公司当接待员，约两周后要求改做全职，在那里工作了六个月。这家公司由加里·马什十八岁时创办，把影视剧本整理成剧情梗概、人物描述等内容的分解表，分发给订阅的经纪人，供他们为客户争取角色。公司在这一领域占据主导地位，但市场有限：订户原则上必须是获得正式认可的经纪人；整个业务也难以监控，分解表在较大的经纪公司里无疑被复印传阅。面对这些经济困境，加里转向了多元化经营。

paras.en: I’d been living in Los Angeles just under a year when, in the spring of 1983, I answered an ad in the Hollywood Reporter for a receptionist and got the job.
paras.zh: 我在洛杉矶住了还不到一年，1983年春天，应征了《好莱坞报道者》上一则招聘接待员的广告，得到了这份工作。

w.m: 《好莱坞报道者》（美国娱乐业刊物）

paras.en: The pay wasn’t much, but the work was in “the Business”—an apt Los Angeles euphemism for the entertainment industry.
paras.zh: 工资不高，但干的是“那一行”的活儿——在洛杉矶，这是对娱乐业的一种贴切的委婉说法。

w.m: （洛杉矶人的说法）那一行，指娱乐业

paras.en: The location was within bicycling distance of my home, and they only wanted someone to work mornings.
paras.zh: 上班地点离我家不远，骑自行车就能到，而且他们只要一个上午来上班的人。

w.m: 在离……（步行、骑车等）可到达的距离内

paras.en: I’d get off by 1 p.m., which I thought would leave me plenty of time to do my own writing.
paras.zh: 我下午1点前就能下班，原以为这样会给我留出大把时间，从事自己的写作。

paras.en: I was wrong about that.
paras.zh: 这一点我想错了。

paras.en: The place was so frantic I’d come out wired and need the rest of the day to simply calm down.
paras.zh: 那地方忙乱得厉害，我每次下班出来都神经紧绷，光是让自己平静下来，就得花掉一天里剩下的全部时间。

w.m: adj. 忙乱的；手忙脚乱的
adj. （口）神经紧绷的；极度亢奋的

paras.en: When, after about two weeks, I realized my afternoons were being spent in activities equivalent to running around the block twenty or thirty times, I asked to be put on full-time.
paras.zh: 大约两周后，我意识到自己的下午都耗在了一些相当于绕着街区跑二三十圈的事情上，于是要求转为全职。

paras.en: Since I wasn’t getting anything else done, why not, I figured, jump in for the total experience?
paras.zh: 既然别的事情我一件也没做成，我心想，何不索性一头扎进去，好好体验个彻底？

paras.en: The (still thriving) company I found myself a part of possessed the unlikely name of Breakdown Services, Ltd.
paras.zh: 我就这样成了这家公司（至今仍生意兴隆）的一员，它有个出人意料的名字：Breakdown Services有限公司。

w.m: adj. 兴旺的；生意兴隆的
发现自己（处于某种境地）；不知不觉成了
adj. 出人意料的；不大可能的
adj. （公司）有限（责任）的（Limited 的缩写）

paras.en: During the six months I worked there, I learned to savor all of that phrase’s more cynical reverberations, but in terms of the job, it dealt with the dismantling or breakdown of television and film scripts.
paras.zh: 在那里工作的六个月里，我学会了细细品味这个名称所有那些更带讥讽意味的弦外之音；不过就工作而言，它涉及的是拆解或者说分解影视剧本。

w.m: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；带讥讽意味的
n. 回响；（喻）余韵，弦外之音

paras.en: Scripts gathered from producers or studios would be regurgitated (回流) by Breakdown in the form of plot summaries, character descriptions, the number of scenes per character, and the number of dialogue lines each speaks.
paras.zh: Breakdown公司会把从制片人或制片厂那里收集来的剧本重新吐出来，形式是剧情梗概、人物描述、每个角色出场的场数，以及每个角色说的台词句数。

w.m: v. （把吞下的食物）吐出；（喻）把（吸收的信息）重新吐出

paras.en: These compilations were then xeroxed and distributed to hundreds of subscribing actors’ agents who proceeded to submit their clients for likely parts.
paras.zh: 这些汇编材料随后被复印出来，分发给数百名订阅了分解表的演员经纪人，经纪人们接着便为自己的客户报名，争取那些可能合适的角色。

w.m: adj. 可能合适的；有希望的

paras.en: It was a process, as I was to discover by way of angry phone calls when “breakdowns” arrived late or not at all, that the agents regarded with a reverence others might reserve for morning prayer.
paras.zh: 每当“分解表”送迟了或者根本没送到，愤怒的电话就会打来，我后来正是通过这些电话发现，经纪人们对这道流程怀着一份虔敬，而别人或许只会把这样的虔敬留给晨祷。

paras.en: Breakdown Services, Ltd., was the brainchild of a young man named Gary Marsh.
paras.zh: Breakdown Services有限公司是一个年轻人的独创，他名叫加里·马什。

paras.en: Gary was twenty-eight when I met him, but he’d founded Breakdown when he was eighteen and was considered something of an entrepreneurial prodigy.
paras.zh: 我认识加里时，他二十八岁，但他十八岁就创办了Breakdown公司，人们认为他算得上是个创业神童。

paras.en: His mother was an agent and he’d observed the piles of scripts she and her agent pals had to plow through in order to match a given role with the talent they represented.
paras.zh: 他的母亲是一名经纪人，他曾看到，为了把某个特定角色和自己所代理的艺人对上号，母亲和她那些当经纪人的朋友不得不埋头啃完一摞摞剧本。

w.m: 费力地读完；艰难地处理完
v. 代理；担任……的代理人

paras.en: He’d also observed how much they hated the reading part of their jobs and had cleverly devised breakdowns as a way of extracting the material they needed.
paras.zh: 他还看出他们有多讨厌工作中要阅读的那一部分，并巧妙地设计出分解表，作为提取他们所需材料的一种办法。

paras.en: By the time I arrived, five full-time breakdown writers worked in a desk-lined back room overlooking a parking lot.
paras.zh: 我来的时候，已有五名全职的分解表写手在一间后屋里工作，屋里排满了办公桌，俯瞰着一片停车场。

paras.en: I’ve heard the current crew has now advanced to computers, but when I was there typewriters were the norm.
paras.zh: 我听说现在那班人已经进步到用电脑了，而我在那儿的时候，打字机还是常规配置。

w.m: n. 一班人；全体工作人员

paras.en: When they weren’t typing, the writers would curl up on the office’s worn stuffed couch and, with a script propped against one arm, fill legal-sized yellow pads with dialogue line numbers and comments which they’d then type up.
paras.zh: 写手们不打字的时候，会蜷在办公室那张磨旧了的软垫长沙发上，把剧本支在一侧扶手上，在一本本法律文书尺寸的黄色拍纸簿上写满台词句数和评语，然后再把这些内容用打字机打出来。

w.m: adj. 有软垫的；填塞了衬料的
adj. （纸张）法律文书尺寸的（8.5×14英寸）

paras.en: It could be a complex job.
paras.zh: 这可能是一项复杂的工作。

paras.en: For example, the breakdown for a film originally called Teenage Gambler lists over forty characters, ranging from the teenaged gambling leader to five waiters who sing “Happy Birthday” at a surprise party.
paras.zh: 例如，有一部电影原名《少年赌徒》，它的分解表列出了四十多个角色，从十几岁的赌博头目，一直到在惊喜派对上唱《祝你生日快乐》的五名服务员。

w.m: adj. 十几岁的；青少年的

paras.en: Perhaps because of the patience involved in this sort of extraction, women seemed to dominate the ranks of the break-downers (during my tenure the ratio was four to one).
paras.zh: 或许是因为这类提取工作需要耐心，分解表写手的队伍似乎以女性为主（我在职期间，比例是四比一）。

w.m: v. 在……中占主导地位；支配
n. （剧本）分解员（作者的戏称，即分解表写手）

paras.en: Although Gary knew I’d done a bit of writing, I was relegated to the front office and never received an invitation to try my hand at breakdowns.
paras.zh: 虽然加里知道我写过一点东西，我却被打发到了前台办公室，也从没受邀去试写分解表。

w.m: v. 把……贬到（较低的位置）；使降级
尝试（做某事）；试一试身手

paras.en: It wasn’t something I really wanted to do.
paras.zh: 那并不是我真心想做的事。

paras.en: For one thing, the writers were a youthful bunch.
paras.zh: 一来，那些写手都是一帮年轻人。

w.m: 一来；首先（用于列举理由）

paras.en: The back room senior was in her early thirties, but none of the others had hit twenty-five.
paras.zh: 后屋里最年长的那位三十出头，而其他人没有一个满二十五岁。

w.m: n. 年长者；资历最深的人

paras.en: And I think Gary rightly surmised I’d be too openly cynical for the job or try to embellish too much.
paras.zh: 而且我认为，加里猜得没错：我要么会太不加掩饰地冷嘲热讽，不适合这份工作，要么会试图过多地添枝加叶。

w.m: adv. 公开地；不加掩饰地
adj. 愤世嫉俗的；冷嘲热讽的

paras.en: Breakdowns were produced anonymously and offered no artistic evaluations of the scripts.
paras.zh: 分解表都是匿名制作的，对剧本也不作任何艺术上的评价。

paras.en: The writers might talk among themselves about a piece they felt was particularly good or bad, but such editorializing was not allowed to make its way into the final product.
paras.zh: 写手们私下里可能会谈论某部他们觉得特别好或特别糟的作品，但这类评头论足是不允许混进最终成品的。

w.m: n. 发表个人评论；夹带主观意见

paras.en: That this restriction was frustrating is indicated by the fact that two of the writers began venting opinions as moonlighting theater critics for small local papers.
paras.zh: 这项限制让人憋闷，这一点可以从下面这个事实看出来：有两名写手开始在当地的小报上兼职当剧评人，借此宣泄自己的观点。

w.m: adj. 令人憋闷的；令人沮丧的
v. 宣泄；发泄（情绪、观点）

paras.en: For Gary, the most problematical aspect of the breakdown business was its limited market.
paras.zh: 对加里来说，分解表这门生意最成问题的一点是市场有限。

paras.en: This had nothing to do with his operating methodology; he did what he could to exploit the possibilities.
paras.zh: 这和他的经营方法毫无关系；他已经尽其所能去挖掘各种可能性。

w.m: v. 充分利用；开发；挖掘

paras.en: Each weekday a hardy crew made predawn deliveries of breakdowns to agents’ homes or offices, while a post-dawn quartet of pager-equipped Breakdown field workers haunted the big studios ready to pounce on an available script.
paras.zh: 每个工作日，一班吃苦耐劳的人员在天亮前把分解表送到经纪人的家里或办公室；天亮之后，由四名配有寻呼机的Breakdown外勤人员组成的小队则频频出没于各大制片厂，随时准备扑向能弄到手的剧本。

w.m: adj. 吃苦耐劳的；能吃苦的
v. 常去（某处）；频繁出没于
adj. 可得到的；可获得的

paras.en: For these studio prowlers speed was of the essence, not only because Hollywood tends to be crisis-prone and wants everything done quickly, but because a rival, spawned by the success of Breakdown Services, Ltd., and infuriatingly named BreakThrough Productions, Ltd., was also on the hunt.
paras.zh: 对这些在制片厂里四处转悠的搜寻者来说，速度至关重要，这不仅是因为好莱坞往往容易出现危机，凡事都要求快速办妥，还因为有一个竞争对手也在四处搜寻：这家公司是Breakdown Services有限公司的成功催生出来的，名字起得让人恼火，叫BreakThrough Productions有限公司。

w.m: n. 四处转悠搜寻（猎物）的人；潜行者

paras.en: Breakdown Services unquestionably dominated the field, but the field itself had immutable perimeters.
paras.zh: Breakdown Services公司无疑在这一领域占据主导地位，但这个领域本身有着不可改变的边界。

w.m: v. 在……中占主导地位；称霸
adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的

paras.en: Breakdown’s subscribers had to be accredited agents, though there were some exceptions to this rule.
paras.zh: Breakdown公司的订户必须是获得正式认可的经纪人，不过这条规定也有一些例外。

w.m: adj. 获得正式认可的；经认证的

paras.en: For instance, specialized media organizations, such as the competitive, vulture-like companies that insured movie productions, could keep tabs on the industry by subscribing to the weekly Breakdown summaries.
paras.zh: 例如，专门的媒体机构，比如那些为电影摄制提供保险、争强好胜、像秃鹫一样的公司，就可以通过订阅Breakdown公司每周的摘要，密切关注这个行业。

w.m: adj. 争强好胜的；竞争激烈的
adj. 像秃鹫一样的；（喻）贪婪掠夺的

paras.en: But the whole Breakdown operation was hard to monitor.
paras.zh: 但Breakdown公司的整个运营很难监控。

paras.en: When I was there, a Breakdown subscription was expensive, something like $500 a year.
paras.zh: 我在那儿的时候，订阅Breakdown的费用很高，一年大约500美元。

paras.en: And though breakdowns were copyrighted and unauthorized reproduction was clearly prohibited, xerox machines are notoriously bad at picking up such distinctions, and among the larger agencies breakdowns were undoubtedly duplicated and passed around.
paras.zh: 而且，尽管分解表受版权保护，未经授权的复制也是明令禁止的，但复印机出了名地不善于分辨这类区别；在那些较大的经纪公司里，分解表无疑被复印出来，四处传阅。

w.m: adv. 出了名地；臭名昭著地
n. 经纪公司；代理机构

paras.en: Gary’s response to these built-in economic dilemmas was to diversify.
paras.zh: 加里应对这些固有经济困境的办法是多元化经营。

w.m: v. 实行多元化经营；使多样化

paras.en: A separate department for commercials, for example, appeared as part of the Breakdown menu.
paras.zh: 例如，一个专做广告片的独立部门出现了，成为Breakdown业务菜单的一部分。

w.m: n. （服务、业务的）项目单；菜单

paras.en: Although Breakdown staffers were supposed to refrain from giving tips to potential talent, I did once tell a friend—who hoped to finance the college educations of her five-year-old identical twins by getting them on a commercial—that a juice company had put out a call for identical twin girls.
paras.zh: 虽然Breakdown的员工按规定应避免向有望成为艺人的人透露内部消息，但我确实有一次告诉一位朋友，说有家果汁公司在公开征召同卵双胞胎女孩。这位朋友希望让她五岁的同卵双胞胎拍上广告，以此为她们上大学筹钱。

w.m: adj. 潜在的；可能成为……的

paras.en: Their agent submitted them, but they didn’t get the job.
paras.zh: 她们的经纪人给她们报了名，但她们没被选上。

paras.en: The nightly Breakdown delivery system expanded to an all-day messenger service.
paras.zh: Breakdown每晚的递送系统扩展成了全天候的专人送件服务。

w.m: 专人递送服务；快递服务

paras.en: Gary also made available an assortment of directories and mailing labels listing casting directors, talent agents, and literary agents in Los Angeles and New York.
paras.zh: 加里还提供各式各样的名录和邮寄标签，上面列有洛杉矶和纽约的选角导演、演艺经纪人和文学经纪人。

w.m: 文学经纪人；著作权代理人

paras.en: The current Breakdown brochure adds yet another Breakdown amenity; for fifteen dollars you can receive an “actors’ relaxation” cassette tape “designed to maximize your abilities and stimulate your creative senses”.
paras.zh: 如今的Breakdown宣传册上又添了一项Breakdown便利服务：花十五美元，你就能得到一盒“演员放松”磁带，它“旨在最大限度地发挥你的能力，激发你的创造性感官”。

w.m: n. 便利设施；便利服务
v. 最大限度地发挥；使最大化
adj. 创造性的；有创意的

passages.name: 2023年 Passage Three
passages.title: 温馨之家与主人的爱妻
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与情感
passages.summary: 叙述者在矿工的简陋木屋里日夜度过了好几个星期，后来来到一处温馨雅致的住所，满心欣喜。主人自豪地告诉他，屋里的一切都是妻子亲手布置的，还引导他发现了妻子的照片，说她回娘家去了，星期六晚上回来。叙述者因届时自己已经离开而深感失望，他渴望见到她，渴望强烈得让他害怕，于是暗下决心为求心安马上离开；主人则一再挽留，说妻子会失望，最后还拿着她的照片让叙述者当面对她说，他本可以留下来见她却不肯。

paras.en: It was delightful to be in such a place, after long weeks of daily and nightly familiarity with miners’ cabins—with all which this implies of dirt floor, never-made beds, tin plates and cups, bacon and beans and black coffee, and nothing of ornament but war pictures from the Eastern illustrated papers tacked to the log walls.
paras.zh: 在漫长的几个星期里，我日日夜夜与矿工的小木屋为伍，对它们熟悉透了——这就意味着泥土地面、从不整理的床铺、锡盘锡杯，咸肉、豆子和黑咖啡，除了原木墙上钉着的、东部画报里的战争图片，再没有别的装饰；此后能置身于这样一个地方，真是令人愉快。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；可爱的
n. 小木屋；简陋的小屋

paras.en: That was all hard, cheerless, materialistic desolation, but here was a nest which had aspects to rest the tired eyes and refresh that something in one’s nature which, after long fasting, recognizes, when confronted by the belongings of art, howsoever cheap and modest they may be, that it has unconsciously been famishing and now has found nourishment.
paras.zh: 那一切全是冷硬、凄凉、只顾物质需求的荒芜景象；而这里却是一个安乐窝，其中的种种景象能让疲惫的双眼得到休憩，也能让人天性中的某种东西重新振作起来——这种东西在长久的断食之后，一旦面对艺术的物件，无论它们多么廉价、多么朴素，便会意识到自己一直在不知不觉地忍饥挨饿，如今终于找到了滋养。

w.m: adj. 只重物质的；物质主义的
n. 安乐窝；舒适的小窝
v. 使休息；使得到休憩
v. 使恢复活力；使振作
adv. 无论多么；不管怎样
adv. 不知不觉地；无意识地

paras.en: I could not have believed that a rag carpet could feast me so, and so content me; or that there could be such solace to the soul in wall-paper and framed lithographs (平版印刷画), and bright-colored tidies and lamp-mats, and Windsor chairs, and varnished whatnots (陈设架), with sea-shells and books and china vases on them, and the score of little unclassifiable tricks and touches that a woman’s hand distributes about a home, which one sees without knowing he sees them, yet would miss in a moment if they were taken away.
paras.zh: 我原先怎么也不会相信，一块碎布地毯竟能让我这般大饱眼福，这般心满意足；也不会相信，墙纸和装了框的平版印刷画，色彩鲜艳的椅背罩和灯垫，温莎椅，上过清漆、摆着贝壳、书籍和瓷花瓶的陈设架，还有女人的手在家中各处布置的那二十来样难以归类的小花样、小点缀，竟能给心灵带来这样的慰藉——这些小花样、小点缀，人看在眼里却不知道自己看见了，可要是把它们拿走，马上就会觉得少了什么。

w.m: 碎布地毯（用碎布条织成的地毯）
v. 使大饱眼福；使尽情享受
n. （椅背、沙发上的）装饰罩；椅背罩
温莎椅（一种木制靠背椅）
n. 瓷器；（作定语）瓷制的
n. 二十（个）；（the score of）二十来个
n. 小花样；巧妙的手法
v. 发觉缺了……；因……不在而若有所失

paras.en: The delight that was in my heart showed in my face, and the man saw it and was pleased; saw it so plainly that he answered it as if it had been spoken.
paras.zh: 我心里的欣喜流露在脸上，那人看在眼里，很是高兴；他看得那样分明，竟像听我亲口说出来似的，答起话来。

paras.en: “All her work,” he said, caressingly; “she did it all herself—every bit,” and he took the room in with a glance which was full of affectionate worship.
paras.zh: “全是她的手艺，”他温存地说，“全是她亲手做的——每一点每一滴都是。”说着，他一眼扫过整个房间，目光里满是深情的崇拜。

w.m: adj. 充满深情的；慈爱的

paras.en: One of those soft Japanese fabrics with which women drape with careful negligence the upper part of a picture-frame was out of adjustment.
paras.zh: 女人们会拿那种柔软的日本织物，看似随意、实则精心地披在画框上部；屋里就有一块这样的织物没有摆正。

paras.en: He noticed it, and rearranged it with cautious pains, stepping back several times to gauge the effect before he got it to suit him.
paras.zh: 他注意到了，便小心翼翼、煞费苦心地重新摆弄，好几次往后退开，估量效果，直到把它弄得合了自己的心意。

w.m: v. 重新摆放；重新整理

paras.en: Then he gave it a light finishing pat or two with his hand, and said: “She always does that.
paras.zh: 然后，他用手在上面轻轻拍了一两下作为收尾，说道：“她总是这么弄。
